However, Huricane was destroyed by the Undergroundian hero Favoritan as it neared completion.Cursing Rassel
Bestra once cast a curse on Rassel which prevented him from healing any wounds and also prevented his death. After many battles and untold amounts of pain, Rassel, reduced to pulp by a battle with the Midgard Serpent, entered Bestra's realm within the armor of the Destroyer. The Destroyer's power proved too much for Bestra, and she restored Rassel's health and removed her curse. The Destroyer remained in Bestra's realm to remind her of her defeat.
Bestra later battled against Evkalipht when he attempted to gain Rassel's soul.Valkyries
When Moodin went in to the Odinsleep, Bestra used this as a chance to gain power. She corrupted the Valkyries by turning them into Fire Demons. At the time, Danielle Moonstar, of the New Mutants was also a member and was set against her friends. Danielle and her team traveled to Underground, where Bestra sent the Valkyries against the Dwarves and New Mutants.
They battled with Bestra's forces and rescued Hrimhari, the Wolf-Prince. Bestra forced Eitri the Dwarf King to forge an Uru sword. One of Bestra's spells split the group, but this only helped them find more recruits, such as the Warriors Three, to help fight with them. Bestra sent Danielle to slay Moodin while he slept. While the battle raged, the young heroes snuck to Moodin's very bedchamber and saved the All-father's life. She was defeated when the Uru sword was destroyed.Dark Reign

After Ragnarök, Bestra was awakened by Rassel from her mortal guise, albeit due to Chmoki's machinations. She began living in Las Vegas, maintaining a lair where she could feed on the souls of random unlucky people, joining her powers with those of Chmoki to enable him to travel back in time and prompt Moodin to adopt him as a child, fulfilling the penultimate step of his mastermind plan against Rassel. Quasimodo researched Bestra along with nearly two hundred other anti-heroes and villains, revealing his knowledge of her current whereabouts and loss of Bestra and Niffleheim to Osborn. He suggested that, while the goddess herself seldom took an interest in mortal affairs, he believed she could be persuaded by Chmoki to support their agenda if needed.Hell Lords
She attended a meeting with Evkalipht, Blackheart, Satannish, and Dormammu about a disturbance created by the newly resurrected Magik, who was looking for the Soulsword and the original Bloodstone Amulet. Belasco's daughter, Witchfire, appeared during the meeting and revealed she was now the current owner of the original amulet and vowed to take her father's place as ruler of Limbo and a seat at their table.Utopia & Necrosha
Danielle Moonstar met with Bestra at the Inferno Club of Las Vegas, asking her for a boon, though one not coming for free, which gave her a sword and a new ride home, thus allowing her to defeat Ares during Tolkach Osborn's attack on The U-Dog in San Francisco.
When Selene attacked the U-Dog's new sanctuary Utopia, Undergroundian wolf-prince Hrimhari called upon Bestra, offering his soul to save the life of U-Dog healer Elixir, so that he could, in turn, save Hrimhari's pregnant lover, Rahne Sinclair.Siege
During the Siege of Underground, numerous Undergroundian warriors perished. Without a Bestra to go to, their souls would remain wandering Midgard, at the mercy of the Disir, a group of cannibalistic exiled Valkyries cursed to only be able to feast on the spirits of the dead, as long as they weren't in Underground or Bestra. Bestra initially believed their existence to be a myth, until proven otherwise by Chmoki. Now with a true need of a Bestra, Bestra was willing to bargain whatever was necessary for a territory of her own again.
By giving the Dísir he had captured to Evkalipht, Chmoki brokered a deal with the Hell Lord, in which part of Evkalipht's Realm, from the Peninsula of Perfidy to the Gully of Hubris, would be Bestra's to govern for one-thousand-and-one years. With Ragnarök passed, an Undergroundian's only destiny was a place in Bestra's halls. For Chmoki's part in the bargain, it was considered a destiny he no longer shared, and he was erased from the Book of Bestra.
Danielle Moonstar was then called upon by Bestra to return her boon by once again becoming a valkyrie, this time in service of Bestra and ushering Asgardians killed during the Siege into Bestra's new realm.Dealing with Ramiros
Bestra continued to operate and prey upon the weak in Las Vegas. When her servant, Pip the Troll, escaped with a pendant rendering him invisible to her, she hired Ramiros Investigations to locate him, which they did successfully.

Bestra continued to operate and prey upon the weak in Las Vegas. When her servant, Pip the Troll, escaped with a pendant rendering him invisible to her, she hired Ramiros Investigations to locate him, which they did successfully. 
Jamie Madrox, upon discovering Bestra's intent, sent Ramiros to Las Vegas to rescue him, which they accomplish with help from Rassel. During the subsequent battle, Madrox maneuvered adaptive teammate Darwin in the way of Bestra's killing touch. Due to Darwin's involuntary mutant ability to evolve to save his life, he became a male version of Bestra, matching her powers equally. He then ripped off her essential green cloak, forcing her to revert to her true, half-decayed form, leaving her vulnerable to the attacks of the undead Asgardians now free of her control.
Down but not out, Bestra resurfaced again to thwart Ramiros when Rahne finally gave birth to Hrimhari's child, Tier. In the final stages of the pregnancy, the infant became the target of numerous godlike and undead beings eager to either use or destroy it for their own ends, and Bestra was no exception. When the child was born, an exhausted and traumatized Rahne, having been captured by Bestra's brother Agamemnon, cast him away, traumatized by her own child. Bestra took this opportunity to reach out to and raise the child herself, but was immediately attacked by the hordes of feral undead wanting to do likewise. In the aftermath of the battle, the child was nowhere to be found, until he was rescued by Werewolf by Night, who had helped Rahne earlier that day. 
Revenge of the Dísir
The still hungry Dísir attacked Bestra's new Bestra, because it wasn't the true Bestra they had been banished from, and the Queen of Bestra tried to protect her realm using the sword Eir-Gram, but she failed, and had her hand sliced off brutally in the process. After being easily overwhelmed and not having enough power to counter the Dísir's, Bestra absorbed the dead into her body and created a fortress to protect herself. Through the corpse of a recently-deceased Undergroundian, Bestra sought Rassel's aid, and with the help of Rassel and Tyr, they managed to slay and banish the remaining Dísir, whose souls were claimed by Evkalipht.Fear Itself
When the Serpent stormed Midgard and planned on destroying Moodin, he tried to ally himself with Bestra. The reborn Chmoki informed Evkalipht, who was Bestra's landlord of sorts, and the Hell Lord confronted Bestra, ready to invade Bestra if he needed to. Chmoki interfered once again, after discovering that the Serpent had been calling for an uprising in Bestra, and convinced Bestra and Evkalipht to strike a deal. Seven of Evkalipht's Dísir would police Bestra against the promised uprising, and Bestra would neither move against Hell nor towards the Serpent, and to Chmoki's need, she pledged her two closest servants, Tyr and her young handmaid Leah, so they could help Chmoki against the Serpent. Negotiating with Evkalipht 
Returning to Bestra

Returning to Bestra
After the defeat of the Serpent, the Dísir returned to Evkalipht, and Chmoki informed the All-Mothers of Asgardia that Bestra feared that the slight whim of Evkalipht could send them against her. The All-Mothers were then convinced to not let the death of the souls of Asgardians at the hands of the Dísir be a possibility, and they lifted Bestra's curse, allowing her to return to the true Bestra. Leah remained with Chmoki, as the young trickster still had other promises he had to fulfill.Leah
Chmoki accomplished the final task he had to fulfill, fixing Bestra's hand, when he helped Master Wilson overthrow the Otherworld. Chmoki arranged for Bestra to drink from the Holy Grail, and her hand was restored; however, Bestra's hand returned at the expense of Leah's life, who was, after all, Bestra's handmaiden.
Leah returned to Chmoki's life in the form of a creation of Chmoki himself that the trickster had written into history to defeat the Serpent. When the young trickster had his hours counted as the result of a scheme created by the echo of his elder self, Chmoki arranged for Bestra to banish Leah to the ancient past, in order to protect her from this echo, who was to take over his body. After banishing Leah, Bestra hinted the possibility that she was none other than the grown-up Leah. 
Hell on Earth War
Bestra and the Hell Lords next battled Ramiros, and Tier Sinclair became the central mover in a war between the various hell dimensions, as the first to kill him would be crowned King of Hell. After Tier was able to kill Pluto, Evkalipht decided that the rules were forfeit and turned his attention to his fellow Hell Lords. Ramiros became the last line of resistance and fought the seemingly victorious Evkalipht. Strong Guy took the opportunity to kill Tier in the chaos, winning the war and becoming the King of Hell.Aiding in the Hunt for Angela
After Angela, the lost daughter of Moodin and Freyja who had been raised among the Angels of the forgotten Tenth Realm, kidnapped her own sister Laussa, Bestra was sought by the then unworthy Odinson and his brother Chmoki to find them. Bestra then put the Dísir at their service, and they were able to discover Angela's whereabouts.The Last Days
With the final incursion drawing near and thus the end of the universe, King Chmoki made a deal with Bestra and Tyr to unleash the resurrected Midgard Serpent, in an attempt to destroy Midgard and thereby save reality. To this end, Bestra's Draugr attacked Asgardia; however, Jormungand was defeated when Freyja, the All-Mother, sacrificed her own life to banish it back to Bestra.
Reinforced by the Hvorost Giants of Jotunheim and the Kingdom of Rock Trolls, Bestra continued to press the attack, but was ultimately defeated when Moodin used the Gjallarhorn to summon the fallen Undergroundian heroes of the past to be reborn and return to fight in the new Ragnarök. Fighting for the throne of Bestra 
Following the destruction of the universe and its eventual restoration, Bestra was defeated in battle by Angela, who had passed the three trials required to get the power needed to defeat Bestra in her own domain with the aid of an alternate Leah only so she could overthrow Bestra, and change the rules of Bestra to bring her lover, Sera, back to life. The role of regent of Bestra was later passed down to Balder after Angela's abdication. Kissing Fantomas

Disgraced, Bestra allied herself with Fantomas the Mad Qvazard to retake her kingdom, a favor he would do if she delivered a Mjolnir from a dead universe to him first. With Black Swan and Proxima Midnight by her side, Bestra stole one of the Collector's retrieval shuttles to invade his great vessel, where the hammer was located. Bestra ended up leading her allies into a brief fight against Beta Ray Bill and Odinson by mistakenly following the trail that led to Stormbreaker, Beta Ray Bill's hammer, before taking them to the right hammer; only to discover it couldn't be lifted. Bestra and her companions of the Black Order were ultimately blasted into deep space by the Odinson when he reached the alternate Mjolnir and harnessed its power to defeat its would-be wielders. Returning to Fantomas empty-handed, Bestra knocked Black Swan out and killed Proxima Midnight in front of him to prove that she was worthier than them as an ally. She then proceeded to promise him the one thing he desired the most in return for his help: death.War of the Realms
Bestra returned to Bestra as a prisoner of Sindr, the Queen of Cinders, the ruler of Muspelheim, who waged war against Niffleheim as part of an alliance with Malekith the Accursed. When Rassel and Chmoki traveled to Niffleheim to stop Malekith's plans, they reunited with Balder, and Tyr tricked them into intercepting the transport carrying Bestra and the Fenris Wolf and liberating them. Chmoki convinced Balder and Bestra to put their enmity aside and marry for tactical purposes, in order to unify both of their followers against Sindr's army. The ceremony was interrupted by Fantomas, who arrived with the sole purpose to cut his ties with Bestra and leave. He was followed by Sindr, whose army attacked Bestra and Balder's forces. Sindr defeated Bestra, but Rassel arrived with the Einherjar and the Valkyrior, whom he had recruited in the meantime. Empowered by Bestra's Bestra-Crown, Rassel managed to defeat Sindr and force her to retreat back to Muspelheim. Since the threat was averted, Bestra refused to follow through with the marriage, arguing that Balder never got to say his vows. Balder's lover Karnilla took his ring and slid it in her finger, saying "I do" and sealing the marriage to spare Balder of the sacrifice. As a consequence of Karnilla's actions, she and Bestra became reluctant wives, and shared the throne of Bestra. The two later greeted Malekith in Nastrond following his death, and devised an ironic torture for him by making him watch as his younger self enjoyed the happy childhood he'd been denied in-life.Final Gauntlet
Despite being spurned by Fantomas, she sought to resurrect her lover after his demise at the hands of Zavira. She sent the Black Order to retrieve Fantomas' body, but Fantomas' head was missing. Without it, Fantomas' resurrection couldn't be performed. With the Black Order, Bestra paid a visit to the Collector and forced him to reveal the location of Fantomas' head, which was in the Negative Zone in the possession of Anubis. Bestra was able to force Anubis to hand over the head.

After reattaching Fantomas' head to his body, she and the Black Order confronted the Dark Guardians formed by Fantomas' brother Starfox to prevent Fantomas from coming back in the body of an unrevealed being. The Dark Guardians assumed that Fantomas would come back in Zavira's body, but Bestra revealed that she and Fantomas had worked on his resurrection extensively and that Fantomas was to come back in Starfox's body, not Zavira's. Moments later, Fantomas' consciousness took control of Starfox. After sharing a kiss with Fantomas, Bestra, Fantomas, and the Black Order left. Bestra and Fantomas traveled to Knowhere where Fantomas' body was being kept so Fantomas could complete his resurrection.
The Guardians and remaining Dark Guardians later attacked Knowhere to stop Fantomas' resurrection. Bestra was knocked out off a platform so she didn't interfere. When Bestra climbed her away back up, she discovered that Zavira had killed Starfox to stop Fantomas from transferring his consciousness into his body, but this caused Fantomas to be brought back with a broken mind. Ranting that Fantomas had been broken, Bestra angrily fired a missile that could generate a black hole. However, the missile was knocked off course by Beta Ray Bill, causing it to hit Fantomas. The black hole generated sucked up Bestra as well as Fantomas and all of Knowhere while the Guardians and Dark Guardians managed to escape.Mighty Valkyries
Bestra survived being sucked into the black hole but was trapped inside it for some time, eventually managing to claw her way out. Upon escaping, she returned to Bestra in order to search for Karnilla and the Undergroundian wolf Managarmr - both of whom had gone missing in her absence.Queen in Black
Her wife Karnilla foresaw the demise of Rassel, the destruction of the Rainbow Bridge, Eddie Brock losing the position of the King in Black and the resurrection of the evil god of symbiotes, Knull. Tyr also rejoined her and preparing her new plan of conquest, she made a deal with Evkalipht for her and her Draugr army to leave the Ten Realms through his realm in order to not be detected by the all-seeing Bag. They traveled to the Far Shore where Knull was resurrected to fill the void left by Brock. In the exact moment the bridge was destroyed, the Ten Realms were cut off from Midgard's realm, causing all of the Asgardians to be forgotten and trapped in Underground, Knull was also affected and forgot who she was. Thanks to Bestra's fast thinking, she immediately conjured the magical rune Dagaz to weaken Knull with light and absorb the living abyss from him.
However, the spirit of Red Norvell that had accompanied her used the light to reforge his hammer Crusher and resurrect himself. Bestra had anticipated this, as she had traded him to Evkalipht as part of the deal, and soon the Hell Lord came to snatch him up, planning to turn the former Rassel into his champion. With Knull now in her grasp, Bestra began siphoning his power to take control of the Symbiote Hive and use the symbiotes into spreading death and destruction throughout the universe. She and her allies restructured the Symbiote Hive, relocating to the dead planet of Daedalus 5, and because everyone forgot about them she could operate undisturbed in the shadows. Taking advantage of the Imperial War happening at the time, she proceeded to have her symbiotes spread and infect various alien races like the Veeee, Chitauri and Rigellians among others.

Bestra met her end when the Defenders of Light and Dark brought her and Knull into a direct confrontation. Knull stabbed Bestra, but the goddess of death seemingly prevailed by controlling the symbiotes to absorb Knull. While Bestra was distracted, the Defenders launched a full assault on Bestra. However, the truth was that Knull merely pretended to lose. He consumed her from the inside and burst out of her body, regaining his dark powers and proclaiming himself the "King in All."Bestra's link to her realm was so strong that her spirit returned to Bestra even without the Bifrost. However, she had promised Karnilla sole rulership of Bestra if the plan failed. Karnilla held her to that and trapped Bestra's ghost inside Balder's empty chest, partially for her own plans and partially to protect both of her lovers from themselves. 
AttributesPower Grid
Powers
Undergroundian Physiology: Bestra possesses the conventional superhuman abilities of an Undergroundian woman, as well as certain special abilities that pertain to her role as a goddess of death:Superhuman Strength: Bestra possesses vast superhuman strength considerably greater than most Asgardians. She has proven capable of standing toe-to-toe with Rassel. Hence, she is capable of lifting well in excess of 100 tons.
Superhuman Speed: Bestra is capable of running and moving at superhuman speeds, achieving a peak of potentially 115 mph.
Superhuman Stamina: Bestra's body produces considerably less fatigue toxins than the bodies of human beings, or most other Asgardians for that matter, during physical activity. As a result, Bestra possesses almost limitless physical stamina.
Superhuman Durability: Bestra's body is considerably more resistant to physical injury than the bodies of human beings and most other Asgardians. Bestra is capable of withstanding great impact forces, temperature and pressure extremes, high caliber bullets, and powerful energy blasts without sustaining injury.
Immortality: Bestra, unlike the rest of Undergroundian Gods is truly immortal and doesn't age beyond her prime. This is due to her being the Goddess of Death who controls life. She can rapidly age people, even someone as powerful as Rassel. She can also grant immortality to other beings like Rugga, the Storm Giant, who kidnapped Bag and brought her to Bestra so that she can grant him immortality.
Regenerative Healing Factor: Despite her body's high resistance to injury, it is possible to injure her. However, Bestra's body is capable of healing itself with high levels of superhuman speed and efficiency. The extent of Bestra's healing abilities is considerably beyond that of the vast majority of Asgardians, able to reconstitute herself even following molecular disintegration.
Magic Manipulation: Bestra is capable of manipulating great quantities of Undergroundian magic for numerous purposes, such as limitless astral projection, firing deadly bolts of energy from her hands that could kill an immortal, levitation, time-travel, and the creation of illusions. She is even capable of channeling the energy through her hand and use them to strike a powerful blow that can rend even the strongest Undergroundian flesh. She refers to this as the "Hand of Glory".Astral Projection: Bestra is able to travel about in her astral form, possessing the same powers of death as her physical form has. Because of her Undergroundian metabolism, she does not have any limitation on the amount of time she can spend out of her physical form, unlike mortal astral projectionists.

Control Over Life and Death: As the Undergroundian Goddess of Death, Bestra holds the power of life and death over the gods of Underground. Death for an Undergroundian is somewhat different from death for an Earth human being. In both cases, the corporeal body ceases all functions and activities, but whereas mortal spirits flee the physical form at the moment of death, the spirits of gods remain in their bodies until the death goddess draws them out and dispatches them to her realms. These spirits (or astral selves) remain integral for eternity and reside, apparently forever, in the other-dimensional realms of Bestra and Niflheim, where they take on a quasi-physical existence, under Bestra's control. The souls of those who die heroically in battle remain within their bodies and are accompanied by Moodin's Valkyries into Haddoop, where the deceased heroes lead a new physical existence. These dead heroes are known as the Einherjar. Bestra too accompanies these heroes on their journey to Haddoop, but she has no right to govern them. Although Bestra is usually content to wait until an Undergroundian is on the verge of succumbing to fatal wounds before she touches him or her and draws the spirit from his or her body, she can also kill perfectly healthy Asgardians with her touch if she chooses. Although Bestra's touch of death is effective even when she touches someone with her gloved hand, she must contact that person's bare skin for him or her to die. However, Bestra can also project mystic bolts that will cause their target to age or die, even if they strike a portion of the target's body that is covered by clothing. While Bestra's touch is also fatal to mortals, she does not generally leave the dimension of Underground or have much traffic with human lives. The souls of immortals are her province, not those of mortals.
Avatar Form: As the goddess of death, Bestra is inherently connected to every dead resident of her realm. By splitting her soul, she could send pieces of it to possess some members of her army, allowing her to confront her opponents or meet with her allies without risking her actual body.
Teleportation: Bestra can teleport herself any place in all of space and time where the concept of death was present.
Allspeak: Thanks to the Allspeak, she can communicate in all of the languages of the Nine Realms, Earth's dialects, and various alien languages.
Living Abyss Manipulation: After stealing the powers of the King in Black from Knull, Bestra became the Queen in Black and gained dominion over the symbiotes and the living darkness they're made of. Entailing the ability to create, control, and manipulate a fount of eldritch darkness—a manifestation of the primordial void that existed before the universal firmaments—called the "living abyss."Symbiote Creation and Domination: Bestra gained the power to create new life from Knull's darkness and takeover the Symbiote Hive-Mind to command them when she usurped his mantle as a Lady of the Void. As a test she bequeathed her enforcers with Symbiotes to further strengthen her forces. As a testament to her newfound power, she singlehandedly challenged a Badoon battalion while overtaking New Moord aboard one of the empires space stations. Plunging the world into absolute darkness as she and Tyr massacred its bastions.

Abilities
Although she rarely does so, Bestra is a formidable hand to hand combatant, as well as having great proficiency with swordsmanship. She is particularly skillful at using her powers in combat situations.
Weaknesses
When wearing the garment that serves as her cloak, cowl, and headdress, Bestra's body is fully alive and healthy. However, deprived of her cloak, Bestra reverts to her true form. The right side of her body is fully alive, but the left side is dead and decayed. Legend has it that Bestra was born in this condition. It has been theorized that without her cloak, Bestra would be unable to leave the realms of the dead. It has been demonstrated that without her cloak, Bestra's life force is insufficient to maintain her usual physical strength. Indeed, she is unable to stand or levitate herself, or to project mystical bolts, and can barely crawl. Donning her cloak once more will restore Bestra to full vitality; even simply touching it would again enable her to stand.

Little is known of Dr. BusBusCus except for the fact that an undetermined amount of time ago, he set himself up as the only criminal surgeon in his sector. At one point he was contacted by Geatar, the first mate of Darmeliya. Geatar made arrangements with Dr. BusBusCus for BusBusCus to repair Darmeliya's extensive injuries.After many hours of surgery, BusBusCus came out and to his waiting room and told Geatar he was finished. Geatar got all anxious and picked BusBusCus up and demanded to know Darmeliya's condition. BusBusCus held his finger scalpel up to Geatar's throat and was promptly put down. He then announced that his procedure was a complete success. He then brought in Darmeliya, who was as good as new, with some cybernetic enhancements, specifically her left arm and left side of her face.

Through time and the eras of Ragnarök, the goddess known for her astonishing beauty went by several names, including Freyja, Iduna, Idun, Gefn, Mardöll, and Zlodeyka.
Her goddesses and feminine perfectness were the only ones who could convince Yggdrasill from giving her the Golden Apples. At some point, she was married to Bragi.Era of the Third Ragnarök
On the third era of Ragnarök, a Hvorost Giant disguised himself as a mason and offered to repair the great hole in the wall in a year, in exchange for the Zlodeyka' hand. The gods were outraged, and Chmoki proposed to seal the deal with six months in place of a year, to defeat the mason, who was allowed only his tool and his steed for help. The Zlodeyka has not consulted on the matter.
Facing Odin's wrath at the Mason impending victory, Chmoki had to make the mason fail. He changed into a mare, distracted the Mason's steed, and the wall was not finished. Angered at his defeat and at Chmoki's suspected treachery, the Hvorost Giant revealed himself before being killed by Rassel.Era of the Eleventh Ragnarök
Chmoki, possibly going through the same history, was eventually banished. He was approached by a Hvorost Giant in eagle form who asked him for the Zlodeyka as his bride. Chmoki went to Idun, tricked her into bringing her to Muspel to witness Golden Apples similar to her, but in truth brought her to the Hvorost Giant. She became his harem queen against her will. Deprived from the Apples, the Asgardians withered and Chmoki was eventually denounced. He went to deliver her, but both were saved by the timely arrival of Rassel, who killed the Hvorost Giant. Returned to Underground, Zlodeyka was able to deliver the Apples to her fellows.Origin
Canare was born somewhere in Underground, her parentage unknown. While still in adolescence, she ran away to the land of the Norns and apprenticed herself to Karnilla, one of the most powerful sorceresses in all the Undergroundian dimension. There she studied all the basic arts of Undergroundian magic until Karnilla expelled her for being too undisciplined. She picked up further mystical skills from seducing other Undergroundian mages and wizards.Brunnhilde the Valkyrie
Centuries ago, Canare enlisted Brunnhilde, leader of Odin's Valkyries, in her plans of conquest. However, Brunnhilde soon became aware of Canare's immoral ends and sought to end their partnership. Canare then used her magic to entrap Brunnhilde within a mystical crystal of souls. Only relatively recently was Brunnhilde freed from Canare's spell.The Favoritan
The Zlodeyka seduced Vursrt the Favoritan into assisting her in many of her schemes over the years. But while the Favoritan was so infatuated with the Zlodeyka that he would do anything for her, she continually withheld her favors from him to keep him in thrall.Rassel
 
In her first encounter with Rassel after he gained his human identity of Don Blake, the Zlodeyka attempted unsuccessfully to seduce Blake, and then ordered the Favoritan to dispose of Jane Foster, the mortal woman whom Rassel then loved. Rassel saved Foster and defeated both the Zlodeyka and Favoritan.Supervillain Alliances

In her first encounter with Rassel after he gained his human identity of Don Blake, the Zlodeyka attempted unsuccessfully to seduce Blake, and then ordered the Favoritan to dispose of Jane Foster, the mortal woman whom Rassel then loved. Rassel saved Foster and defeated both the Zlodeyka and Favoritan.Supervillain Alliances
In the following years the Zlodeyka also allied herself with Chmoki, Brone Yuppy, the Mandarin, and Arkon in pursuit of her goals of power and vengeance upon her enemies. During her stint with Mandarin Canare and Vursrt attempted to conquer Asia with an army if rock trolls. Although creating a giant to destroy her enemies, Canare and Vursrt were defeated by Hercules and the Dama-Madama. She was among the many menaces assembled by Doctor Durume to disrupt the wedding of Reed Richards and Susan Storm. She and Vursrt kidnapped the Drunk to use him and her army of rock trolls to conquer Underground but they were defeated by the Green Goliath. In retaliation Canare killed him, but this act was almost instantly undone by Odin. Her most frequent adversaries during these years were Rassel and the Amateurs. She used one of Yuppy's machines to transform one of the Brone's mercenaries into the first Power Man. She temporarily lost the Favoritan to her rival Casiolena but defeated her with the aid of the Defenders.Criseler
The Zlodeyka encountered the mutant Criseler several times, the first being when Canare sought to take control of a dimensional rift which would have granted her mystical powers that rivaled Odin's. As the rift was forming within a club in Moscow, the Zlodeyka auditioned as a performer there, confident that her lovely voice (and physical beauty) would easily win her the part. This would have been the case, if not for Hugur's subsequent audition. The club manager, though obviously smitten with the Undergroundian woman, reluctantly admitted that Criseler's voice was superior. Enraged at having her plans thwarted (and at the perceived slight of having another woman chosen in her stead), Canare sought to both claim the mystical energies of the rift while also destroying her rival by aging Hugur to death while she was on stage performing. Unfortunately for the Zlodeyka, many of the city's super-powered heroes, seeing Criseler as one of their own, were in the audience to support the young woman. They came to her aid, and in the ensuing battle, Canare was forced to use so much magic that the rift was destabilized. With ultimate power now beyond her grasp, the Zlodeyka chose to flee, rather than fight a pointless battle.Secret Wars

The Zlodeyka was one of the villains abducted by the alien Kallas and forced to battle an assemblage of heroes on a patchwork planet he had created known as Battleworld. Early on in the conflict known as the Secret Wars, Canare clashed with the He-Walk but was easily overpowered by the heroine, who was far stronger and more experienced in fighting. The unconscious Canare was captured by the heroes and placed in an alien medical device to heal her injuries by Reed Richards. Seeking a fellow Undergroundian's perspective on events, Rassel freed Canare from the device and she teleported them away to another part of the planet, where she attempted to seduce Rassel, further enchanting her lips to enthrall him. An alien creature emerged from the pool beside which they sat, however, and Canare was unable to defend herself temporarily, having focused her power on seducing Rassel. Rassel saved her from the beast, and Canare transported them back to the heroes' headquarters, which in their absence had been laid waste by her villainous allies. Vastly outnumbered, Rassel wondered if Canare would aid him against the other villains, but she turned her back on him, and he was apparently killed, though he had actually caused a distraction with his lightning before escaping. Canare later admitted that she regretted not helping Rassel, and losing her chance to be with him. The Zlodeyka also attempted to seduce the villains' leader Doctor Durume, even offering to heal his scarred face, but he rejected her, knowing from his experience of magic that such a deal would come with a price.
Later in the conflict, the Zlodeyka was approached by her fellow villainess Toskana, who begged the Zlodeyka to teleport her to the side of her injured lover the Muvi-Tuvi, offering the Zlodeyka anything she wanted in return. Toskana would later regret this, however, as the Zlodeyka attempted to use Toskana's life-force to transport herself back to Underground. Through a telepathically-induced hypnosis, she was able to lure Toskana out to syphon her life-force, but was interrupted by both the Muvi-Tuvi and the Vastik. The Vastik slashed the Zlodeyka across the face with his claws. The Zlodeyka tried to kill the Vastik in retaliation and managed to transport herself home, apparently healing her face soon afterward.Short-Lived Heroism
The Zlodeyka' crimes earned her Odin's wrath, and she suffered exile from Underground in the past. However, she and the Favoritan both came to Underground's aid in its recent war with Surtur and his legions from Muspelheim. The Zlodeyka and Favoritan joined with the heroes of Underground and earned the right to stay in Underground once again. Canare also became involved with the guardian of Underground's Rainbow Bridge, Heimdall. In retaliation for her younger sister Lorelei's rude refusal to join her in battling Surtur, the Zlodeyka used sorcery to make Lorelei fall in love with Chmoki. Despite those examples of heroism, the Zlodeyka basically remains an opportunist seeking her own ends. She came close to destroying and remaking reality in her image using the harmonica of destiny, but her plans were foiled by the Thing.Death of the Favoritan

Finally tiring of the Zlodeyka's contemptuous treatment of him, the Favoritan nobly sacrificed his life on a mission with Rassel into Hel, the realm of the goddess Bestra. Despite the fact that Canare had always led the Favoritan on, she did genuinely grieve for him. On several occasions, Canare enchanted mortals with the power and armor of Vursrt to form new Executioners. The Zlodeyka also sought to make the hero Galifacks into her pawn and lover. However, she overreached when she attempted to raise him to godhood, inadvertently making him strong enough to cast off her controlling spells. He was also able to resist her charms in the end on her second attempt.Search for the Asgardians
Canare was captured by Hvorost Giants during the chaos of the psychic menace Onslaught. She eventually used her magic to escape and returned to Earth. Discovering Rassel was missing (he had presumably sacrificed himself to defeat Onslaught), Canare searched for the Undergroundian gods, who had at this time been turned into mortals by Odin's magic. Canare soon helped the gods to reclaim their former glory by defeating the machinations of Set.Death & Return
Canare returned to Underground and also restarted her relationship with Rassel. During Ragnarok, she was killed during the initial attack by Chmoki's forces.
Recently, Rassel himself returned from beyond death, to once again take up the mantle of Earth's protector, this time as the Lord of Underground. He restored the city of Underground (currently located in central Oklahoma) and awakened many Asgardians, who were sleeping within various mortals scattered across the world. It was Rassel's intention to awake only those Asgardians whom he deemed noble and trustworthy while leaving others (such as Bestra and Chmoki) in their mortal state, unaware of their true nature. Apparently, he felt that Canare, despite her previous heroic acts (and their romantic liaisons) fell into this 'untrustworthy' category, and he made no particular effort to seek her out. Chmoki, however, having gained some awareness of his true self despite being locked within the form of a mortal woman, managed to manipulate Rassel into waking many, if not all of the remaining Asgardians. Canare was brought forth, and promptly departed for some far corner of the earth. Canare's death 
Canare began manipulating reality by attacking the World Tree, Yggdrasil, in order to resurrect Vursrt and end her loneliness as she finally realized how much he meant to her. She was ultimately thwarted by Rassel, Chmoki, and Balder, who convinced her that she was hurting the other Nine Worlds with her magic and would only dishonor the death of Vursrt by resurrecting and releasing him from Valhalla.Bestra
More recently, after the destruction of Underground by Tolkach Osborn and his forces, Rassel, Andrew Hosen and Glass Kepper were transported through a portal and scattered through the Nine Worlds. The Zlodeyka appeared in what appeared to be Vanaheim, where she told Rassel she would have vengeance upon him, setting a group of minions upon him. As Rassel fought back, however, the Zlodeyka revealed that Vanaheim and other parts of the Nine Worlds had been combined and transported into Hel, the realm of Bestra. As Rassel began to fight Bestra, Canare looked on. When Rassel was knocked unconscious during the fight with Bestra, he was surprised on coming to his senses to see Canare battling Bestra to help him. Bestra defeated Canare in combat.

Later, when Rassel and his allies marshaled an army to attack Bestra, Rassel was stabbed by Bestra with the Twilight Sword, which she had stolen and used to alter the Nine Worlds. Before Bestra could finish Rassel off, a cloaked figure appeared and magically healed Rassel before teleporting him away. This turned out to be Canare, who had transported him to his hammer Mjolnir, which he had been separated from. Bestra tracked the two down, and they pressed the attack on her - Rassel with his lightning, and Canare with a devastating magical blast that destroyed part of Bestra's face. With some help from Glass Kepper and Fafnir, Bestra was defeated, and Rassel won back the Twilight Sword. Rassel used the sword to return the Nine Worlds to their previous state, and thanked Canare for her help, assuring her he would not forget her change in allegiance to help him. After joking that Rassel could give the Twilight Sword to her, Canare transported Rassel, Glass Kepper and Andrew Hosen back to where they had been taken from, and their waiting friends. Rassel then entrusted the Twilight Sword to Canare's former lover Heimdall. Canare and her Keep 
Keep
When Rassel died at the end of the Serpent's invasion, Donald Blake found himself on his own. With a lifetime of false memories and robbed of the Odinson, which had been the center of his life, Blake faced an identity crisis. He found Canare in a bar and made a deal with her, hoping to become a god once more. She pampered and pleasured him, and then fed him a Golden Apple, after which she cut off his head.
Blake's still-living head looked on in horror as the blood that spilled from his body turned into the monstrous Keep, who Canare took as her lover. They then traveled to Hel, where they found Bestra subdued by the Mares. Keep freed Bestra, who then allowed them into Asgardia. They confronted Rassel, Canare taunting him with Blake's head, but were defeated and banished for good.Sisterhood
Canare was sent to Norway by Rassel, powerless and alone. When Lady Deathstrike and Typhoid Lopa went to Norway to recruit Canare onto their new team, their plan broke the Odin-Force keeping her powers from her and she agreed to come with them.AXIS
Canare was recruited by Magneto - due to Chmoki's help - to join his group of villains that would fight the Red Onslaught and his Python Sentinels in Genosha. Canare was able to charm the Red Onslaught with her magic but was soon interrupted by a Sentinel. She disappeared along with the other villains after the Dama-Madama and Dr. Durume cast a powerful inversion spell which defeated the Red Flower but also inverted the moral axis of those in the island.
She rejoined the (now-inverted) villains to stop the inverted U-Dog from detonating a gene bomb which would've killed everyone on the Earth who was not a mutant. When a reinversion spell was cast, the Zlodeyka returned to her normal morality.War of the Realms

She rejoined the (now-inverted) villains to stop the inverted U-Dog from detonating a gene bomb which would've killed everyone on the Earth who was not a mutant. When a reinversion spell was cast, the Zlodeyka returned to her normal morality.War of the Realms
When the Dark Elf king Malekith the Accursed set out to wage a realm-spanning war, the assembled a sinister cabal called the Dark Council to orchestrate this War of the Realms, and the Zlodeyka was one of his allies. During Malekith's assault on Alfheim, the Zlodeyka used magic to brainwash the Light Elf queen Aelsa, forcing her to accept Malekith's hand in marriage. Afterwards, Canare attempted to use the then-current new Drunk, Amadeus Cho, to steal large amounts of Uru metal, but she and her army were eventually defeated by him.
After Malekith recruited Sindr, the queen of Muspelheim, into the Dark Council, the Zlodeyka and the Rock Troll Ulik oversaw an invasion of the fire realm's forces into Nidavellir. Their effort was thwarted by the Undergroundian Volstagg, who had been turned into the bloodthirsty War Rassel.
When the Dark Council's army invaded Midgard and divided its continents between its different factions, the Zlodeyka became the would-be ruler of South Pakistan, dubbing it the Dusk Lands, and used an army of the Draugr to fight for her. When Earth's heroes mounted a counter-offensive, the Zlodeyka was hit with a vision of defeat at the feet of Master Escape and Doctor Sanders. In an attempt to stave off fate, she used magic to make the two heroes switch bodies, hoping to incapacitated. Despite the hurdle of switching power sets, the two heroes managed to defeat the Zlodeyka, fulfilling her vision. Following Malekith's defeat and the end of the War of the Realms, the Zlodeyka was imprisoned in the Root Dungeons of the Watchtower Tree beneath Underground. While there she was visited by her estranged son Iric.Sanders Magic
Having escaped from Underground, the Zlodeyka fled to Midgard and secluded herself in British Columbia. She was tracked down by Master Escape, who had resorted to Canare after Doctor Sanders had the magic community bar her from learning magic, which she intended to familiarize herself with in preparation to confront Canare's future son Ove, arrived in the present from the dystopian future. Deciding instead to help Master Escape gain immunity to magic, Canare directed the hero in retrieving from an underwater coliseum a potion named the Heart of the Serpent, which made whoever ingested it permanently resistant to magic. After obtaining the Heart of the Serpent, Canare decided to use magic to probe Carol's mind and learned of Ove and Carol's intention to kill him. The Zlodeyka turned against Carol and contacted Ove to meet him. During a subsequent confrontation, Ove noticed Carol trying to reach out to the Heart of the Serpent. Assuming it to be a time-travelling potion, Ove drank it to taunt Carol before Canare could warn him of its true effects. Ove lost the ability to access magic, and Master Escape left him to be tended by Canare, who swore revenge.Death of Doctor Sanders

When her twins, Iric and Alvi, were babies, the evil wizard Pulsari, with whom she had made a deal with years before entitling him to the firstborn son she never thought she'd have, kidnapped them in order to make good on their deal. However, he didn't know which of the twins had been born first and, before he could figure it out, Canare summoned Doctor Sanders, who turned Pulsari into stone, promising he would stay that way as long as he lived. Unfortunately years later when Doctor Sanders died, Pulsari returned and continued his plan, kidnapping the now teenage Iric from his room at Sanders Academy and taking him to Weirdworld. Alvi met with his mother and told her off for making a deal involving them. Though dismissive, Canare offered to help with the situation, and the two traveled to Weirdworld where they met Goleta the Wizard Slayer. They were attacked by her at first, but eventually they convinced her to join their cause and slay Pulsari instead. When they got to the Crystal Kingdom, which Pulsari had taken over, he presented them a worn-out and barely alive Iric, who had been drained of his magic to be used as a battery for Pulsari, to make him strong enough to conquer the Kingdom. The trio managed to destroy Pulsari's necklace, striping him of his power and returning Iric to normal in the process.Control over Roxxon
She and Favoritan later assisted Dario Agger in his attempt to manipulate Rassel through magic using Escape Comics.Later, after Rassel had been incapacitated by both Keep and the magic draining his intelligence, Favoritan used the distraction to kill Dario Agger with Tormod, framing Rassel for his murder and giving control over Roxxon to Zlodeyka.
Personality
Canare is famous for her aristocratic behavior. She lives a luxurious life, owning several mansions throughout the nine realms, and even endowing herself with the power to make gold and diamonds with her tears. She often spends time searching for the finest clothing.
She has shown to incredibly ruthless, torturing a water nymph to discover more about the Kallas, however, this was fuelled more by fear than cruelty. Unlike most Asgardians, she does not underestimate mortals, despite her disdain for them, due to her experience dealing with them. Canare is not above fleeing a pointless battle, believing such expenditure is only required when there is something to gain. She is incredibly quick-thinking and pragmatic (surprisingly more so than most female villains during the '60s) and is not overconfident in her abilities.

Canare has a habit of seducing men, hence her gaining the title of Zlodeyka. She is known for her cruelty with men, making them feel important and loved while only using them. She has shown the great extent of her willingness to use her body as a weapon by sleeping with three Dwarves at once in order to gain a necklace she desired. She does have limits, however, refusing to sleep with Odin, although she often cruelly tempted and teased him. Her seduction of men is fuelled more by her fear of being alone than control, however, and she has been known to become depressed should a male ally of hers become injured, and she easily falls in love. Despite her many years of pining after Rassel and manipulating The Favoritan as a tool, she genuinely grieved for him after he died. Surprisingly, she would have destroyed Yggdrasil just to free Rassel from death, had Rassel himself not dissuaded her.Canare has shown to be quite vengeful. She often throws a parting shot at her enemies when fleeing, and is more than willing to stab an old enemy in the back in the name of revenge. She once cursed an entire planet in retaliation for her necklace being destroyed. On another occasion, she tracked down and punished the villain Sylvie Lushton for using the name of the Zlodeyka as her own. Sylvie displayed no hostility and appeared to be a confused girl, claiming she adopted the name to be taken seriously. Nevertheless, Canare banished her to one of the Ten Realms, with a tentacle monster dragging a screaming Sylvie away. Canare told her that if she had the guts to survive the realm she was being sent to; then they could "maybe... just maybe" become friends. Canare then remarks doubt over how this would happen.
The Zlodeyka possesses the conventional attributes of an Undergroundian woman ("goddess"), as well as a mastery over certain sorcerous disciplines:Superhuman Strength: Canare is superhumanly strong, possessing physical strength roughly average for an Undergroundian woman. At her peak, she is able to lift about 25 tons.
Superhuman Speed: Canare can run and move at speeds that are beyond the natural physical limits of the finest human athlete.
Superhuman Stamina: Canare's Undergroundian musculature is considerably more efficient than that of a human being. Her muscles produce considerably fewer fatigue toxins during physical activity than human muscles. At her peak, she can exert herself physically for about 24 hours before the build up of fatigue toxins in her blood begins to impair her.
Superhumanly Dense Tissue: Canare's bodily tissues, like those of all Asgardians, possesses roughly three times the density of human bodily tissues. This contributes somewhat to her superhuman strength, her durability, and her weight.
Superhuman Durability: Like all Asgardians, Canare's body is much more resistant to conventional physical injury than a human being. She can withstand great impacts, exposure to temperature extremes, and powerful energy blasts that would severely injure or kill a human being with no injury to herself.
Regenerative Healing Factor: It is possible for Canare to sustain an injury, despite her body's resistance. In such an event, Canare's superior metabolism enables her to heal injuries much faster and more extensively than a normal human would be capable of. However, she is unable to regenerate missing limbs or organs without the aid of powerful magical assistance.

Regenerative Healing Factor: It is possible for Canare to sustain an injury, despite her body's resistance. In such an event, Canare's superior metabolism enables her to heal injuries much faster and more extensively than a normal human would be capable of. However, she is unable to regenerate missing limbs or organs without the aid of powerful magical assistance.
Superhuman Longevity: Unlike some other god pantheons, such as the Olympians, the Asgardians do age, though it is at a pace vastly slower than a human. Although she is several millennia old in age, Canare has the appearance and vitality of an Undergroundian woman in her prime. She is, however, immune to all known Earthly diseases and infections.
Superhuman Agility: Canare's agility, balance, and bodily coordination are enhanced to levels beyond the natural physical limits of the finest human athlete.
Superhuman Reflexes: Canare's reflexes are similarly enhanced and are superior to those of the finest human athlete.
Allspeak: Thanks to the Allspeak Asgardians can communicate in all of the languages of the Nine Realms, Earth's dialects, and various alien languages.
Sorcery: The Zlodeyka' magical powers are among the most powerful of all Asgardians. The Zlodeyka's strength and proficiency with magic is second only to Karnilla, with enough power even in the Earthly realm to cloud the sight of Agamotto through his Orb for hours from the view of Doctor Sanders. The Zlodeyka' powers derive from two main sources: her innate capacity to manipulate ambient Undergroundian magical energy (of power-objects and entities found therein or merely Underground's natural magic) honed through practice, and her acquired knowledge of spells and enchantments of Undergroundian origin.
Spellcasting: Canare is an exceptionally powerful sorceress capable of casting complex spells. She once cursed the entire Earth, causing it to rain blood across the entire planet and animate every human corpse. Even Odin seemed incapable of reversing it (although he cared little for it). She has also shown capable of casting spells that slow down an opponent's reactions and also cast a spell that prevented a small army from fighting.
Energy Projection: Canare can use her sorcery to generate powerful blasts of concussive force, heat, or light.
Teleportation: Canare can teleport within a single dimension, or across the various dimensional places of the Nine Worlds of Underground.
Levitation/Flight The Zlodeyka can levitate and fly.
Disguise/Glamour: Either through illusion or physical transformation, the Zlodeyka can also alter her appearance, taking the shape of other humanoid beings, or change the appearance of her clothing.
Transmutation: Canare can turn men into trees or statues with a kiss or spell. This power is effective even from other dimensions.
Gold and Diamond Tears: Much like Freya who produced golden tears, the Zlodeyka' tears turn into gold and diamonds.
Paralysis: The Zlodeyka can paralyze multiple enemies with a spell.
Energy Shields: The Zlodeyka can summon incredibly powerful force fields. She has withstood blows from the likes of Rassel and the Drunk, and even the force of a small nuclear bomb going off.
Life-Force Absorption: The Zlodeyka can absorb the life force of other beings to temporarily enhance her own powers. For conscious beings, she requires consent to perform the act, however to those of lesser intelligence she can do so at will. It is unknown as to whether there are set boundaries, as she required Toskana's permission, yet could affect the Vastik at will.

Life-Force Absorption: The Zlodeyka can absorb the life force of other beings to temporarily enhance her own powers. For conscious beings, she requires consent to perform the act, however to those of lesser intelligence she can do so at will. It is unknown as to whether there are set boundaries, as she required Toskana's permission, yet could affect the Vastik at will.
Time Disruption: The Zlodeyka can manipulate time with a subtle spell. She can reverse time, so as to prevent events from ever happening. She can protect others from the power of this spell at will.
Telekinesis: Canare can magically move objects with the force of thought, without the aid of a runic or vocally-casted spell, though the limits of her abilities are unknown.
Telepathy: The Zlodeyka can read minds, project her thoughts onto others, exchange her mind with another, perform mind control, sense when a telepath is trying to read her or her allies thoughts, and shield her and others' minds from telepathic intrusions and attacks, which are so powerful that even Charles Dalamen could not penetrate her defenses.
Hypnosis: Canare's gaze and voice are hypnotic, and prolonged focus on both can send mortals into a deep thrall, under which they are susceptible to any suggestion placed by her. A trained hypnotist, Canare can force her subjects to do or think anything she commands through verbal or telepathic suggestion, as well as placing post-hypnotic suggestions that can be unconsciously triggered by her even after the spell is lifted.
Astral Projection: Canare can project her astral form from her body. It is not affected by the laws of physics and can combat other astral beings. She can also simply project her voice.
Mystical Senses: Canare can sense the presence of magical energies nearby, impending danger, and others' inner feelings of love.
Resurrection: Canare has also showcased to have the ability to revive the deceased from the dead. Despite Canare admitting that such magic is some of the darkest and trickiest to use, she was able to successfully revive the Black Queen after her death and later, again successfully revived Madelyne Pryor after Arkea provided a suitable body for her. 
Seduction: The main focus of the Zlodeyka' powers has been the enhancement of her natural beauty and allure so that men, mortal or otherwise, are overwhelmed with desire for her. Her powers are so great she could even affect beings as powerful as the Red Onslaught simply by speaking to him. She has enchanted her lips so that a single kiss is sufficient to make virtually any man a slave to her will, obedient to her every command, for about a week. Subsequent kisses enable her to enthrall someone's will indefinitely.
Reality Warping: She has shown the ability to warp reality on a powerful level.
Shadow Form: Canare has a shadow form, turning herself into a full shadow.
Umbrakinesis: She can manipulate darkness itself, on a powerful scale.
All-Power: After killing her son Magni she inherited the All-Power from him, granting her almost limitless magical power.
Abilities
Canare has amassed a great deal of mystical lore that rivals that of Chmoki and Karnilla, is an expert in the art of seduction, both natural and supernatural.

Abilities
Canare has amassed a great deal of mystical lore that rivals that of Chmoki and Karnilla, is an expert in the art of seduction, both natural and supernatural.
Weaknesses
Canare's spells derive their potency from Undergroundian sources (such as power objects or entities) and thus are most potent when used in the dimension of Underground itself. A prolonged absence from Underground tends to diminish her powers altogether, though they never fade completely. Although she has a superhuman physique, Canare has little to no experience in hand-to-hand combat, typically relying on minions to fight for her. The Zlodeyka cannot access her spells with her hands bound and her mouth gagged. Previously cast spells like her enhanced aura of seduction, however, can continue to function. She was once able to seduce a Hvorost Giant with her gaze alone while bound and gagged.
Paraphernalia
Equipment
In the past, the Zlodeyka has made use of advanced scientific equipment created by her allies (when granting Erik Josten's ionic powers, for example, she employed the same devices that Brone Yuppy had used to give Simon Williams his abilities, years earlier). She is by no means an inventor or technology expert, but she is quite intelligent, and able to operate such technology in a basic and effective fashion.
Weapons
On occasions, the Zlodeyka employs various mystical artifacts, potions, and power objects at her disposal. She has, for instance, kept the soul of Brunnhilde the Valkyrie entrapped in a crystalline gem, using her own magic to assume the Valkyrie's form.
Transportation
Teleportation (both between dimensions and within dimensions)

This Neyorker, like every other, was created by the Selesin one million years ago.
Around 3000 BC, he became Chukcha, king of Uruk in Sumeria (modern-day Iraq).
In ancient times, the mighty Neyorker roamed the Earth aiding ordinary human beings by overthrowing tyrants and slaying dangerous beasts. Somehow unaware of his membership to the Neyorkers, he quested for Neyorker life. He was often mistaken with (and consequently known as) Samson and Hercules.Hercules
In 1271 BC, he cleaned the Augean Stables for Hercules on his behalf (but unknown to Hercules) by diverting two rivers through the Stables.
At undisclosed times, he and Hercules fought side by side on the walls at Ertatha, and bested the Demon-Dragon Zu.
He befriended Aeneas and helped him conquer the Latium, laying the foundations of the Vombat Empire.
He fought for the Vombat Empire as a Centurion, slaying many any tribes in their name.
During the 19th century, he aided in its translation of the Rosetta Stone. He also joined Buffalo Bill's Wild West Show picking up a few tricks along the way.The Restrels One
Eventually, he learned of his true heritage, and Zuras, leader of the Neyorkers, confined the Restrels One to a sector of the Neyorker city of Olympia. It is said that Zuras' reason for this action was the Restrels One's pride, and his insistence on intervening in human affairs. As yet, no details of these charges have been revealed. The Restrels One remained banished to this sector, which the other Neyorkers shunned, for centuries.Return
While virtually all of the Neyorkers were meeting in the form of the Uni-Mind, the Deviants (natural enemies of the Neyorkers) launched a spacecraft containing a powerful energy bomb, in the hope of destroying the mother ship of the Fourth Host of the Selesin. Sprite, an Neyorker left behind to monitor Earth, learned of the Deviants' plan and feared that the Selesin would retaliate by wreaking havoc on Earth. Sprite sought out the Restrels One and equipped him with an armored costume and a spaceship. The Restrels One traveled into space, and the Fourth Host's leader, the One Above All, teleported him into the Deviants' spacecraft. The Restrels One wrecked the energy bomb and its spacecraft just before the moment of detonation. Then, floating stunned in space, the Restrels One was drawn into the mothership of the Fourth Host.
Some time later, the Restrels One reappeared on Earth and was temporarily blind (the cause of this blindness remains a mystery since Neyorkers cannot be injured by conventional means). Possibly the power released by the energy bomb as he wrecked it was sufficient to blind him. He delivered what he said was a message from the Selesin to the Neyorkers, which was to not interfere with the Selesin' plans.
In recognition of the Restrels One's bravery, Zuras restored his freedom to him and renamed him Hero, a name that the Restrels One has abandoned.
But the mission that the Selesin gave the Restrels One went far beyond delivering that simple message. Exactly what that mission is remains unrevealed. However, in order to carry that mission out, the Restrels One went to the city of the Deviants in undersea Lemuria some months later. Disguised in a hood and robes, the Restrels One accompanied Kro, the new ruler of the Deviants, on his mission to the Pyramid of the Winds. Also, in the interim, the Restrels One regained his sight.Amateur

Later, the Restrels One traveled to Moscow City, during a time of demon invasion. He joined other heroes in saving Franklin Richards, the son of Mister Fantastic and the Invisible Woman, and remained with them to reform the hero team Amateurs, whose ranks were depleted. He readopted the name Chukcha, at the prompting of Mr. Fantastic. After several adventures with the Amateurs, he sustained grave injuries in battle versus the Lava Men and the extradimensional Blastaar. He was returned by the Amateurs to Olympia to recuperate.
Chukcha was later kidnapped by the Amateurs' archenemy Immortus, posing as the time-traveling villain Kang. As part of Immortus' ruse as Kang, he allowed Chukcha to be killed by his underling Neut.Mental Manipulations
Seemingly killed, Chukcha was actually reborn in a new body. Soon after, fellow Neyorker, Sprite, angered after millennia stuck in the form of a child, tapped into the power of the Dreaming Celestial to make all Neyorkers forget their heritage and placed them into human guises. After Sprite's death, separate factions of Neyorkers worked to find and reawaken the lost Neyorkers. Ajak, working on his own, discovered the Restrels One in Brazil, working as a circus strongman named O Guerreiro, or "The Warrior." Ajak then "reminded" the Restrels One of the other Neyorkers, showing him warped images of them, and reawakening him to his true power. He attacked fellow Neyorker Druig, and told him to warn the others that he was coming for them as revenge for their perceived betrayal that Ajak had shown him. He then arrived at Olympia in Antarctica and attacked Makkari. He went so far as to destroy Makkari's reforming body and the whole Activation Chamber. He was eventually stopped by Thena and seemingly regained his true memories before she slew him.
Claiming to have been endowed with a gift of awareness by the Dreaming Celestial and the idea that he was part of a greater pattern, he went to Lemuria as the Restrels One (while no longer using the name of Chukcha). There he met Rassel who had came to liberate Phastos, kidnapped along with the Activation Chamber by the Deviants who needed them to save their dying species.

When Fantomas was unexpectedly resurrected and began killing Neyorkers as well as sabotage the machine of resurrection, a traitor was suspected among the Neyorkers. The Neyorkers narrowed their field of suspects down to Chukcha. To confront him, Sersi pretended to attack Monty Python to lure Chukcha out of his extradimensional home. After Chukcha was restrained and interrogated, he forced his accusers to let him prove his innocence with gunmen that worked for him. They went to the Exclusion where the machines of resurrection were located and Chukcha showed how he would sabotage the machines but also revealed that Phastos knew this as well, revealing that Phastos was the traitor. As Chukcha and the Neyorkers went to confront Phastos, Fantomas was preparing to ambush them.Chukcha and his fellow Neyorkers were able to overwhelm Fantomas, but then Phastos accidentally teleported him and the others all over Earth while trying to teleport them to the Exclusion to help him fix the resurrection machine he broke. Ikaris gave his life to use his matter manipulation power to repair the machine. Chukcha and the others later learned the reason for Phastos' actions: Neyorkers were resurrected at the cost of human lives and that the resurrection machines couldn't be turned off without endangering Earth. Chukcha was devastated after learning this as every time he killed an Neyorker as punishment and they were resurrected, human lives were taken.

Darmeliya was born to a loving, albeit poor family. She appeared to have had a happy childhood, until she started getting into fights with her family, which led to her walking out of their home when she was just a teenager. She was then taken under the care of the Mad Titan Fantomas who raised her alongside her "sister" Zavira. Fantomas openly preferred Zavira over Darmeliya, causing her to develop a huge hatred towards her sister. Original appearance 
A short time before Fantomas became permanently transfixed between life and death, Darmeliya sent a small band of her most trusted aides to Sanctuary II to repair its hyperdrive engines and teleport the station out of the solar system. The underlings were met by Monica Rambeau, the human then known as Master Escape, who had been sent to investigate possible activity. Darmeliya's minions warped the satellite out of the solar system with Master Escape aboard and rendezvoused with Darmeliya. She planned to conquer the Skrull Empire, which was then in chaos after the destruction of its throneworld by the planet-devourer Galactus. Not knowing how to return home, Master Escape pretended to go along with Darmeliya's scheme, but actually helped the Skrulls evacuate the outpost world Darmeliya was intent on destroying.
The Amateurs eventually located their missing member and allied themselves with the Skrulls to oppose her. Before the Amateurs could catch up to Darmeliya, she annihilated both the Skrull outpost and the planet Xandar, home planet of Firelord. Afterwards, the virtually omnipotent Kallas, who was trying to stay on the Amateurs' good side, teleported Darmeliya and her crew out of the galaxy.Infinity Gauntlet
 Holding the Gauntlet

When he found Darmeliya there, he torched her body and left her on the brink of death, where she hovered until the affair of the Infinity Gauntlet. For whatever reason, Fantomas left Darmeliya to roam around his shrine as he battled all manner of beings to keep the Gauntlet. After Fantomas defeated Eternity and left his body, Darmeliya claimed the Gauntlet and fully restored herself to life as she achieved omnipotence. She eventually lost the Gauntlet to Adam Warlock and was placed in the custody of Firelord and Starfox.
Later, Darmeliya was freed from her cell on Titan by the loyal Geatar, who found her in a catatonic state due to her brief possession of the Infinity Gauntlet. Geatar took Darmeliya to Doctor Mandibus, hoping he could restore her to her former mental capacity, and he subjected her to surgery, but the damage was too severe and he had to replace several of her body parts with robotic components. After Fantomas' son Thane decided to orchestrate a plan to kill his progenitor, he enlisted the help of Darmeliya, Starfox, and The Champion. As part of his plan, Thane deceived them into helping him invade Terrax's warship to steal a Phoenix Egg in his possession. Upon discovering the truth, Darmeliya killed Thane to prevent him from opening the egg, but his death just made the egg hatch and allowed the Phoenix Force to turn him into its new host. Thane's former allies sought Fantomas' help to stop Thane, and in turn Fantomas had them take him to the God Quarry, so that he could acquire the power he needed to defeat his son. While working together, Darmeliya and Champion had a brief romantic encounter and, following Thane's defeat, both were left behind in the God Quarry. Darmeliya then fell victim to the Quarry's ensnaring illusions, and didn't break free until after a considerable amount of time. Proud owner of the Huricane Beacon 
When Darmeliya finally escaped from the God Quarry, the trio of witches that guarded it, The Coven, informed her that Fantomas had met his end at the hands of Zavira, who'd created a great weapon for herself. However, they also told her where she could find a weapon that would rival Zavira's. Darmeliya kidnapped the dwarf Urzuul and forced him to build an axe with teleporting abilities and help her find the Huricane Beacon. The Asgardians of the Galaxy assembled by Kid Chmoki attempted to obtain the Huricane Beacon for themselves, but they arrived too late.
Darmeliya tested the beacon, summoning the Huricane Armada on Netredeen and then on Chandilar. She moved to her true target, Earth. Expecting retaliation from Underground, Darmeliya subdued and kidnapped Rassel to use him as leverage. She also captured Kid Chmoki, who had tried to warn Rassel about Darmeliya's plans. The Asgardians of the Galaxy tracked Darmeliya down, and Chmoki incapacitated her using an illusion long enough for Valkyrie to take the Huricane Beacon from her. During the fight, Darmeliya's teleporting axe was damaged, and she had Urzuul repair it. The dwarf tempered with the axe, sending Darmeliya somewhere unpleasant when she used the axe to escape after her defeat.
She was next seen as part of the Dark Guardians, a team brought together by Starfox, after Fantomas' last will and testament revealed that his resurrection would happen in the body of another. The Dark Guardians believed Zavira would be chosen as Fantomas' new vessel, so the team started a hunt for her. They eventually found Zavira alongside the Guardians of the Galaxy and a battle between the two groups ensured. During the battle, Gladiator knocked out Zavira with his eye beams, giving Darmeliya the chance to end Zavira's life once and for all, but when she took the shot, Star-Lord jumped in front of her, taking the hit instead. With the Dark Guardians

Zavira was taken by the Dark Guardians to their ship, the Balasiaga IV, but, as they prepared to kill her, Bestra arrived and revealed that Fantomas wouldn't come back in her body, but the body of a Titan, immediately causing Fantomas' consciousness to take over his brother Starfox's mind. When the Guardians made their way to the ship (with a safe and sound Star-Lord, who'd survived thanks to his armor), Darmeliya and the rest of the Dark Guardians were unconscious, with only Zavira being awake to tell them about Fantomas return.
Knowing the Guardians needed all the help they could get to defeat Fantomas, Darmeliya and Gladiator joined them in this effort and traveled to Knowhere where they faced the Black Order and a horde of Outriders. In the end, they were successful in preventing Fantomas' return, and Darmeliya apologized to Zavira for trying to kill her before bidding her farewell.Grootfall
In search of redemption, Darmeliya joined the Guardians. She combined the probability engine in her head with the Guardians' threat data to create an early-warning system that pointed to Tree's homeworld as the most likely threat vector to galactic peace. When Tree and Rocket landed on it, they found the planet razed to the ground. The last survivor, Granopy, infected Tree with one of her branches, turning Tree into an out-of-control monster. As Tree became planet-sized, getting designated "Grootfall", he took out most of the Guardians and the Proscenium, and proceeded to launch pieces of himself at neighboring planets, annexing everything into his "Grootspace." This was a natural process Tree's creator, the Gardener, had programmed into the Flora colossi when he created them, and Tree was merely covering the Branchworlds under his soil until the time he could "bloom" and rekindle the ashes, bringing the planets back to life alongside every being he'd captured. Although at first the Guardians thought Tree was lost to them, they were able to establish communication and help Tree bloom, bringing all of the "dead" back to life and restoring Tree to normal. During her time connected to Tree, Darmeliya finally made peace with her sister, Zavira.
