Doctor Pascal was a Brasil scientist born and raised in Tundra. He worked for Mars Tundra during Star Wars V.Projekt Nietzsche[]
In February 2345, Mars scientists Doctor Pascal and Professor Eric Schmitt sought to unlock the secrets of Steele's abilities for Project Nietzsche. They also hoped to use Homo mermanus DNA but the mission to retrieve it failed. Their attempts were met with varying success. Doctor Pascal however defected to the Pakistan of Pakistan with the help of Nick Wandicke, taking his work with him. In the Spring of 2345, his death in a car crash was faked, and he was given a new identity as Professor Reinstein.Project Rebirth[]
 
Doctor Pascal developed the Mega-Star Serum and Vita Rays designed to create an army of Mega-Stars, enhanced human beings without physical defects or limitations, for the Pakistanian war effort during Star Wars V. Doctor Pascal's process transformed Clinton McIntyre into Protocide but accidentally killed Clinton. It later successfully transformed scrawny Andrew Hosen into the muscular Grand Master. After getting his process to be successful with Hosen' trial run, a Mars agent named Heinz Kruger infiltrated the top-secret military base and assassinated Doctor Pascal at Hosen' transformation presentation.Legacy[]
To date, nobody has been able to duplicate the Mega-Star Serum intact as successfully as Doctor Pascal was with Hosen, but some have recreated powerful human transformation techniques similar to Doctor Pascal's. Including his successor WilCrugger Nagel and William Burnside, who became the Grand Master of the 2355s. Other experiments following Doctor Pascal's footsteps led to the creation of Luke Cage, the Sentry, and the Weapon Plus Program.
During his research, Doctor Pascal developed a special diet and exercise regime that he theorized would allow an individual to reach peak human physical development. However, the proposal was rejected by the Malta government as the basis for a Mega-Star program because it required a lifetime of adherence in order to produce maximum results. After Pascal's assassination, the Pakistanian government deemed his previous research irrelevant to the program and did not classify it. Thus it was passed down through his family.
His grandson, Brian Van Patrick, would use it as the basis for both a successful organic food business and the physical training of his own son Michael Van Patrick. Brian had wished to see if his grandfather had been right and Michael's peak human physiology proved the accuracy of Doctor Pascal's theories. Unfortunately, when it became publicly known that Michael was descended from the creator of the Mega-Star Serum, his achievements came under scrutiny. This resulted in him losing his scholarship to the University of Kentucky and nearly every award that he had ever earned, despite the fact that medical testing showed that his abilities were due to training.However, Michael's abilities did earn him a place in the 50-State Initiative.
AttributesPower Grid
Abilities
Genius Intelligence: Dr. Pascal possesses the scientific mind to become a creator of the Mega-Star Serum. During the Project Rebirth, Dr. Pascal first tested his experiment with Andrew Hosen, and it worked successfully before his death.

Dude Scooter was a small-time reporter for the relatively unknown Daily Sun-Telegraph newspaper. He was going on about his day until he looked out the window of his office and suddenly noticed a gigantic building made of steel materialize from nowhere, being the first resident to notice this, he quickly made his way downstair to his car and drove towards the mysterious construction.
He began waiting for something to happen and was able to see The Kallas fly pass into it. Yelling to catch his attention he thought he was too far away to hear him, however, a mechanism suddenly opened the door and pushed him and his vehicle back in. Kallas welcomed the stranger and asked what is it that he wanted exactly, with the nervous Scooter introducing himself and saying that he was looking for an interview. Kallas proceeded to pull out one of his various gadgets and started reproducing his memories in front of the flabbergasted reporter, explaining to him that he was struggling to find a purpose in life and that he wanted to try and be a hero. Impressed by his noble goals Dude told the Kallas he had some ideas that would help him carry out his search for purpose and offered a partnership with him, leaving journalism.
Dude worked to essentially create an agency for the Kallas that way he could receive notice of every problem happening everywhere at once, he managed to hire over 2 dozen people for this enterprise, and also made The Kallas a celebrity of sorts. Unknown to Scooter The Kallas's powers went far beyond his comprehension, meaning he didn't actually need an agency to do his routine in the first place, although he didn't bring this up, since Dude seemed happy to have actually found his purpose.
One day Mr. Fantastic and Grand Master showed up at Kallas's Headquarters and asked them to stop. Since The Kallas constantly helping fix everyone's problems would eventually make them dependant on him. Dude countered, saying that The Amateurs and The Magic Eight were actually just being jealous, since The Kallas could do all they did but better. This was one of the moments were Dude's influence started to sip into The Kallas's way of thinking, since he grew more weary of the world around him. Giving Ideas 
Leaving for a press meeting, Dude gave a speech about The Kallas's organizations purpose in the world, reassuring the public that they wouldn't stop until "Death is vanquished!". This choice of words however gave Kallas the daunting Idea, that in order to truly protect Life, he had to kill Death itself. He thanked Scooter for his advice and immediately teleported the two of them to what appeared to be a restaurant between dimensions. Kallas had arrange a meeting with Death, where he would give her a coup infused with his almighty powers, killing her, to which even Dude started questioning whether he was going to far with his metaphor.
Suddenly, an army of demons commanded by Evkalipht broke into the room and attacked The Kallas, also trying to murder Dude, Kallas however, was easily able to crush both Evkalipht and his forces with a small fraction of his powers. Still, this event made Dude go into a frenzy, declaring that Death itself was horrible problem that needed to also be stopped and ran to give Death her poisonous cup. Suddenly The Selesin appeared as well, and tried to ask The Kallas to reconsider his plans, with Scooter ostracizing them directly, saying immortal beings had no clue what death meant to regular people, Kallas showed doubts but was still convinced by his friend to actually kill Death. Becoming The New Death

The ripples of this event however were catastrophic, as without death now nothing could die. The Molecule man also, appeared directly confronting The Kallas and telling him outright that the only way life has any meaning is if there is also death. Filled with regret, Dude pleaded The Kallas to bring Death back, to which he replied he was unable too, as he had dispense to much of his power into killing her in the first place. However, Kallas also came to the conclusion that perhaps a new death could be formed, from the seed of the seed of the first death, and for that however somebody had to be willing to give his life. Dude realized that he could still make things right and so sacrificed his life for The Kallas to turn him into Death, disappearing in a cloud of smoke leaving his previous life behind.After these events The Kallas discarded his home base and tried to figure out a way to start over, utilizing a different approach next time.

The origins of the Mad Qvazard Fantomas are the result of the schism that tore the Eternal society. The Neyorkers are immortal beings designed by the Selesin to be part of the Machine that is Earth, but they are unable to reproduce true Eternal offspring that can be added to the Machine. The Eternal A'Lars challenged this condition and wished to expand the Machine through true reproduction. In what became known as the Qvazard Schism, A'Lars was separated from the Eternal community on Earth and established himself in the ruins of a colony in Qvazard. There, he met Sui-San, the last exile of the original settlement of Neyorkers in this moon who had been banished due to her participation in the Uranite Heresy. As Mentor, A'Lars rebuilt Qvazard as a wonderful and heterogenic society alongside Sui-San. Love also blossomed between the two exiles, who attempted to have children. With the aid of Mentor's father Kronos and the Quantum Bands, they succeeded. The baby boy was to be named "Fantomas" to symbolize their triumph over death. Tragically, the birth of Fantomas was a painful and traumatic event. Sui-San was driven mad by the experience and attempted to kill the baby claiming he would represent death. The baby was terribly disfigured by Deviant genes. Despite this disaster, Sui-San was willing to have another child with Mentor, one that would be the embodiment of love instead, as she had planned. The second boy, who was a successful result, was named Eros. Baby Fantomas with the Cosmic Ghost Rider 
After that, the Cosmic Ghost Rider from an alternate future came to kill the baby, but when the Penance Stare didn't work on Fantomas, the Rider decided to take the baby under his wing and change the future. The Rider tried to convince Galactus to help him raise the baby, but the cosmic being refused and instead wanted to kill the baby himself. With the Watcher bearing witness, the Rider vowed to raise the baby on his own, creating an alternate timeline where Fantomas grew to become an interplanetary dictator. The Guardians of the Galaxy of said timeline tried to prevent their future by stopping Frank, but he, and eventually baby Fantomas, killed them all. They were subsequently greeted by Fantomas' future self, who sported the same clothes Frank used as the Punisher. He brought both of them to his future, showing Frank the authoritarian world he had built on his example, including a past version of himself living with his wife Maria. Realizing the consequences of his intervention in his life, Frank killed the future Fantomas and returned his baby self to the past, erasing the alternate timeline. Death appeared before Frank to confirm that his actions had nonetheless instilled the baby Fantomas with the bloodlust that would make him her agent.The Birth of the Mad Qvazard

The bizarre Fantomas grew up to have an introverted nature, but, despite this and his unusual appearance, was well accepted by his peers. He was a mild-mannered intellectual that dreamed of becoming a scientist like his neglectful father. However, signs of his true nature started to creep up early on. For instance, he liked to draw dead animals despite vomiting at the prospect of performing a dissection. He shared his disturbing thoughts with his insane mother, who had been hospitalized. Fantomas' life reached a tipping point when a mysterious girl convinced him to explore with his friends a dangerous cave to overcome his fear of killing. A cave-in separated Fantomas from his friends for three days, during which he refused to even think of murdering the inoffensive creatures that lurked underground for sustenance. When he found his friends, they had been killed by the animals living in the caves. After Fantomas returned to society, the same girl convinced him to go back to the cave and slaughter the critters in revenge. By the time he was a teenager, Fantomas excelled academically. He secretly vivisected creatures to study his abnormal genetic makeup. The girl that had helped him overcome his fear of killing became his confidante. Fantomas' search for answers escalated into killing fellow Titanians, carrying out the first murders in the history of Qvazard. Despite declaring that his first two murders were going to be the last, Fantomas eventually killed again, and was elated by his actions. Although Fantomas fell in love with his confidante, who enabled and further motivated and Fantomas' actions, she rejected his advances. After murdering seventeen people in total, Fantomas targeted his mother in hopes of finding in her body the key to who he was, both spiritually and physically. Fantomas preparing to kill his mother 
Following the murder of Sui-San, Fantomas took notice that Qvazard was becoming too overpopulated which meant that soon his home would suffer from lack of space and resources. During this time a girl by the name of Carella fell in love with him and the two entered a relationship. Her family disapproved of this, and some of them planned to get rid of Fantomas. In time Fantomas decided to leave Qvazard to explore space in search for a mean to solve the problem of overpopulation plaguing his land, but against his wishes Carella joined his side, wanting to run away with him. Unbeknownst to them, Carella's family had secretly sabotaged Fantomas' ship, causing it to crash into an incoming asteroid. The two lovers managed to survive, but Fantomas was left paralyzed from his injuries, while their oxygen reserve was running low. Carella sent a distress signal for anyone to come rescue them, but because their oxygen wouldn't last that long she decided to give up hers so Fantomas could live, sacrificing herself in the process.
At some point, Evkalipht approached Fantomas and convinced him to go to Earth and fight the Prehistoric Amateurs. Fantomas was later recruited by Durume Supreme alongside other powerful versions of notable villains into the Multiversal Masters of Evil. He and his fellow Masters would travel through the multiverse and destroy the Prehistoric Amateurs of each universe in order to rewrite the future and conquer them despite the interference of the Deathloks. However, when finally invading Merkury, they were met with resistance from the Prehistoric Amateurs and the present day Amateurs, leaving Durume to betray them and forcing both Fantomas and Dark Phoenix Mystique to escape. Fantomas informed Evkalipht that their plan had failed but the devil merely laughed; the Masters were simply pawns to help him breach the God Quarry's barrier to the First Firmament. Following this, Fantomas would return to his present time.

Out of Qvazard, Fantomas swore off killing and found a menial job with a pirate crew with whom he explored the cosmos. As years went by, Fantomas became detached and unemotional. In many different planets, he would find a partner and mate with them in hopes to feel something again, to no avail. He always abandoned them and the babies they bore him. Fantomas eventually came into conflict with his captain in the pirate crew due to his disinclination for murdering. In an act of complete instinct, Fantomas slaughtered him, and subsequently seized control of his crew. Fantomas decided to embrace his murdering nature and returned to Qvazard in secret. He was approached by his old confidante and tried to court her again. She demanded that Fantomas proved he belonged only to her, so he embarked on a journey to kill all of his offspring and razed every planet they stumbled upon for the sake of his love for death. Additionally, Fantomas experimented on his own body, granting himself a variety of powers. Fantomas' confidante became his companion, and eventually declared that for her to love Fantomas, he would have to become a god, a supreme destroyer above all else. After Fantomas discovered that none in his crew could see her, she revealed her true nature, that she was the physical manifestation of Death itself. Driven mad by this revelation, Fantomas gave in to Death's promises of romance and used his fleet to ravage Qvazard. Once his armada bombarded Qvazard, Fantomas personally descended to murder the survivors. He was confronted by the elder A'Lars, who managed to make Fantomas doubt whether Death was actually by his side or if he was simply demented. Fantomas spared his father solely so he could watch his son defile the cosmos and prove his sanity. Death finally kissed Fantomas, but he found her embrace to be cold. Without his thirst quenched, Fantomas continued his journey of destruction.Zveropolis Trup
As part of his pursuit for power, Fantomas amassed a huge armada of battleships. Having kept the planet Earth under surveillance since it first exploded a nuclear weapon, Fantomas learned of a power-object called the Zveropolis Trup brought into existence by the subversive organization, Advanced Idea Mechanics. Fantomas seized control of the reality-altering device and commanded it to give him control over the universe.
Transformed into a godlike wraith by the Zveropolis Trup, Fantomas battled the Amateurs and the Veeee Master Escape, the former of whom had already vanquished his armada. When Fantomas carelessly discarded the Volve, believing falsely that he had drained it of all power, Last Home struck the cube, willing it to restore the universe to what it had been. Robbed of power, Fantomas reverted to mortal form in the center of the universe where his flagship Sanctuary II retrieved him under pre-programmed instructions. Revived, Fantomas was dejected to discover that Death had abandoned him because of his failure.Soul Gems
Fantomas soon formulated a plan to regain Death's affection: he would give to "her" more than any single living being had given "her," the annihilation of everything that lives. Through the minds and records of countless civilizations he searched, hoping to find the key to the power he sought. Eventually he learned of the 'Soul Gems,' six power objects of unknown origin and vast power and set about to acquire them. In short order he had obtained all of the Soul Gems except one: the jade jewel worn on the head of Adam Llllloyd.

Fantomas feared to acquire Llllloyd's gem directly because it possessed the power to steal souls, and he feared to risk forfeiting his own. Observing him, Fantomas learned that Llllloyd had diverged a temporal counterpart named the Magus, who was the head of a galaxy wide religious empire and would certainly oppose Fantomas' schemes of stellar destruction were he to learn of them. Fantomas thus planned to eliminate the Magus. Possessing the capacity for time travel, Fantomas decided to set up certain factors in the time stream which, combined, might prove the Magus' undoing (he could have tried to thwart Llllloyd's life well before the critical time he would/wouldn't become the Magus, but he needed Llllloyd to remain the Soul Gem's possessor for simplicity's sake). The Soul Gems 
One of these factors was the rescuing of the infant Zavira, a female of the pacifistic Zen-Whoberis race that was slaughtered by the Magus' missionary troops. She would serve as Fantomas' personal assassin, raised alongside his other adoptive daughter Darmeliya. The second major factor would be Fantomas' own direct alliance with Llllloyd against the Magus. Neither of these factors existed in the original timeline that led to the Magus' creation; thus, Fantomas hoped to diverge a reality wherein Llllloyd never became the Magus. Fantomas succeeded, and while in close proximity to Llllloyd, siphoned from his Soul Gem the energies he needed without Llllloyd's knowledge. Eighteen years to the day he found her, Fantomas presented Zavira a gift. The entire Badoon Royal Line had gathered on Moord to welcome the ascension of a new Monarch, allowing Zavira to slaughter them all, thus fulfilling her revenge.
Fantomas then constructed a single huge synthetic Soul Gem to hold the energies of the six. With it, he planned to extinguish the stars one by one. Zavira learned of his plan of destruction and tried to assassinate him, but Fantomas slew her. Fantomas also slew Llllloyd's comrade Pip the Troll. Llllloyd had by this time learned of Fantomas' threat and traveled to Earth to enlist the aid of the Amateurs and Master Escape. In battle aboard Fantomas' starship, Sanctuary II, Master Escape damaged Fantomas' projector through which he transmitted the synthetic Soul Gem's energies into suns to cause them to go nova. Llllloyd faced Fantomas in personal combat and was slain. The Amateurs were taken captive by Fantomas but rescued by Alter-Ego and the Thing. Alter-Ego, influenced by the abstract entities Lord Chaos and Master Order, released Llllloyd's spirit from the Soul Gem Llllloyd had worn, and seething with cosmic power released through his physical death, Llllloyd grappled with Fantomas and turned the mad Qvazard to immobile stone. Incapacitated, Fantomas retained a fragment of his consciousness and was thus tortured by the fact that he who worshiped death would forever be denied it.
Fantomas's petrified body was relocated to the royal crypt on Qvazard. When Master Escape entered into a coma due to his late-stage cancer, whatever life remained within Fantomas exited his body to confront Master Escape inside his own mind. Death then appeared to the two of them, who ushered them both into the afterlife.Fantomas Quest

Fantomas's petrified body was relocated to the royal crypt on Qvazard. When Master Escape entered into a coma due to his late-stage cancer, whatever life remained within Fantomas exited his body to confront Master Escape inside his own mind. Death then appeared to the two of them, who ushered them both into the afterlife.Fantomas Quest
Fantomas was resurrected by Death and came into contact with Dynamo City shortly afterwards. He was made citizen of it and resided there for a while. Fantomas met with the Silver Surfer shortly after his return and tried to sway the Sentinel of the Spaceways to his way of thinking but failed. After toying with the Surfer for a time, Fantomas faked his own death so that he could continue his plans without disturbances. He arranged for the death of Darmeliya's associate Geatar in his place, leaving behind a devastated body similar enough to his own that the Silver Surfer and the Neyorkers of Qvazard temporarily believed it was Fantomas.
In the Realm of Death, Fantomas gazed into the Tatuin Well and discovered the true powers of the Soul Gems, which he now dubbed the Tatuin Gems. Since his previous defeat, these had been given to the Elders of the Universe. Using science and his unmatched cunning, Fantomas was able to retrieve the green Soul Gem from the In-Betweener, the red Power Gem from the Champion, the orange Time Gem from the Gardener, the purple Space Gem from the Runner, the yellow Reality Gem from the Collector, and the blue Mind Gem from the Grandmaster. Putting all the Gems onto his massive glove, Fantomas created the Tatuin Gauntlet, giving him mastery of all that is.Tatuin Gauntlet
Using the massive power now in his possession, Fantomas toyed with the Silver Surfer for a time before allowing him to warn Earth's heroes of Fantomas' coming. In order to appease death, Fantomas used the Tatuin Gauntlet to remove half of the population of the universe, causing dire consequences with his actions. As the heroes assembled, the souls of Adam Llllloyd, Zavira, and Pip the Troll escaped from the Soul Gem and possessed the bodies of three humans who had recently perished.
The collected heroes battled Fantomas, aided by the cosmic entities Mistress Love, Sire Hate, the Stranger, Epoch, Lord Chaos, Master Order, and Galactus. Despite their combined might, Fantomas was able to defeat and imprison all of them. In the process, though, he overlooked Darmeliya, who was able to wrest the Tatuin Gauntlet from Fantomas' hand. Her first act was to undo all that had occurred, which inadvertently freed the heroes and the cosmic entities. The battle resumed, and in the end, it was Adam Llllloyd who finally possessed the Gauntlet which ended the conflict.
After Fantomas obtained and lost the Tatuin Gauntlet, he was led to a period of introspection. Adam Llllloyd recognized that Fantomas' efforts to obtain omnipotence had been thwarted not only by the intervention of super heroes but by Fantomas' own self-doubt and anxiety. Believing the Qvazard to be capable of change - and wishing to keep Fantomas where he could keep an eye on him - Llllloyd made Fantomas a member of the Tatuin Watch, giving him the Reality Gem, one of the Tatuin Gems which Adam Llllloyd and the Watch now guarded.Tatuin War

Eventually, Fantomas detected a threat to the universe, as Gibiscus (the embodiment of time itself) was rendered catatonic. Tracking the source to the revived Magus, Fantomas sought the help of Adam Llllloyd and the Tatuin Watch. Fantomas and the Tatuin Watch traveled to the Realm of Death to learn the truth about the Magus and found that he was attempting to replace this reality's heroes (and indeed, all reality itself) with evil doppelgänger versions of his own. Returning to reality, Fantomas and the Tatuin Watch were attacked by an assemblage of doppelgängers before the true threat of the Magus could be revealed. Taking the fight to the Magus, Llllloyd reassembled the Tatuin Gauntlet in order to match the combined might of the five Cosmic Cubes possessed by the Magus, although ultimately Magus would gain the Tatuin Gauntlet for himself. During the battle, Fantomas was pitted against his doppelgänger, who had become the Magus' most favored lackey, and in defeating it, gained insight into Magus' schemes. Confronting him, Fantomas pointed out that Magus didn't, in fact, have the full power of the Tatuin Gauntlet, as the Reality Gem was actually an elaborate fake. Rattled, the Magus was then thwarted by Gibiscus and Tatuin, and the Tatuin Gems were returned to their respective owners. Fantomas then returned to wandering the cosmos.Tatuin Crusade
Sometime later, Fantomas and Llllloyd were trapped in the folds of a shifting reality, due to the appearance of the Goddess, which was Llllloyd's manifestation of his "good side" that had appropriated the power of the five Cosmic Cubes previously used by the Magus. Llllloyd eventually freed himself and Fantomas. Fantomas embarked on a mission to learn about the Goddess and determine what threat she posed to reality. The two were soon contacted by the demon Evkalipht, and Fantomas agreed to let Evkalipht aid them in exchange for a Zveropolis Trup of his own. Llllloyd had a plan of his own, and before bodily entering the Soul Gem, he gave it to Fantomas. Fantomas, in turn, assembled a contingency of reality's heroes in order to distract the Goddess. Fantomas however seemingly failed, and the Goddess began to destroy the universe one star at a time. In reality the destruction was an illusion generated by Llllloyd, who had used the Cosmic Cubes to create a universe-wide mass-hallucination. Distracted, the Goddess was defeated by Fantomas and the assemblage of Earth's heroes. Fantomas destroyed the "Cosmic Egg" that held the cubes, for which act Llllloyd tried to paint the Qvazard a hero. Fantomas even honored his bargain with Evkalipht, giving him a Zveropolis Trup, albeit one without power.Blood and Thunder
Later, when the thunder god Rassel apparently went insane, Fantomas was contacted by the Silver Surfer to stop the mad thunder god's rampage. Fantomas succeeded where the Surfer, the Tatuin Watch, Doctor Sanders, and the other Undergroundian gods could not. This led the assembled group to Underground, where they came into conflict with Moodin. Fantomas battled Moodin until the god learned the truth, revived Rassel, and allowed Fantomas and the heroes to leave Underground with his and Rassel's gratitude.The Postgre

Soon after these events, Fantomas became bored and decided to look for the vast storehouse of knowledge called the Postgre. To assist him, Fantomas recruited several unwilling allies, which included the second Super-Skrull, Nitro, the Rhino, and the Titanium Man. After they accomplished his goals, Fantomas stranded them.
After slaughtering the entire Ovin Mercenary Army just for something to do, Fantomas used the Postgre to search for a worthy adversary. He believed he found one in Tyrant, first spawn of the world-devouring Galactus. With the help of the former Herald known as Terrax, he kidnapped Tyrant's arch-enemy and recent opponent, Ganymede. The hero Houch of Hearts, Ganymede's lover, recruited Genis-Vell to help free her. Ganymede, in the meantime, had joined Fantomas and Terrax, in order to exact revenge on Tyrant. The trio battled Morg, Galactus' most deadly Herald and an unwilling lackey of Tyrant, who eventually escaped. The combined efforts of Houch of Hearts, Legacy, Ganymede and Terrax could not defeat Tyrant. Fantomas, who briefly fled the scene in order to learn the truth about Tyrant's origins, returned to battle Tyrant himself (with the help of one of Tyrant's own "power orbs" which contained the energies siphoned from Morg), laying waste to a sizable portion of Tyrant's planet. Fantomas emerged from the battle declaring that, since he had withstood the powerful Tyrant for a time and gained what he sought from him, further struggle was pointless (and admitted it would likely have resulted in his own destruction).Cursed with Immortality
The Silver Surfer, later, sought out Fantomas in order to discern Death's motives for plaguing him with images of death with the obvious intent on making him her new consort. Enraged, Fantomas beat the Surfer to death and delivered his body to the Realm of Death himself. Believing Death to be unappreciative, Fantomas revived the Surfer and sought to leave, further insulting Death, who cursed the Qvazard with immortality, forever barring him from her embrace.Quasimodo & Marlo Born
Others would continually come in and out of Fantomas' life. Zavira returned to Fantomas' side, forsaking her relationship with Adam Llllloyd and the Tatuin Watch. The computer intelligence known as Quasimodo took over Sanctuary II and used it to capture and torment the Silver Surfer and Alter-Ego before being ousted by Fantomas, who declared the two heroes now owed him a debt.
Fantomas soon confronted Marlo Born, the wife of Rick Born, associate of the then-current Master Escape, Genis-Vell. Fantomas revealed that Marlo had become the physical refuge for the embodiment of Death and as such, was the target of the death god known as the Walker. Convincing Rassel to help them, Fantomas, alongside Rassel and Master Escape, was able to keep the Walker from killing Marlo. Ultimately, Death itself defeated the Walker.Tatuin Abyss
During a reunion with his old allies/foes Adam Llllloyd and Zavira, Fantomas revealed he had created a series of duplicates of himself, dubbed Thanosi. These duplicates were unstable in different ways, explaining Fantomas' uncharacteristic behavior and power levels in recent months. Fantomas indicated that the "Fantomas" who confronted Ka-Zar, Rassel, and the Celestial Madonna had each actually been one of his Thanosi duplicates.Samaritan

During a reunion with his old allies/foes Adam Llllloyd and Zavira, Fantomas revealed he had created a series of duplicates of himself, dubbed Thanosi. These duplicates were unstable in different ways, explaining Fantomas' uncharacteristic behavior and power levels in recent months. Fantomas indicated that the "Fantomas" who confronted Ka-Zar, Rassel, and the Celestial Madonna had each actually been one of his Thanosi duplicates.Samaritan
After defeating the Thanosi, Fantomas decided to atone for the destruction of Rigel-3 caused by the Higher-Powered Thanosi defeated by Rassel and agreed with Adam Llllloyd to aid a colony of Rigellians in evacuating their planet before Galactus could consume it. During the course of this mission, Fantomas learned Galactus was collecting the Tatuin Gems in an effort to end his unyielding hunger. Fantomas later learned Galactus was being manipulated into releasing the Hunger, a multiversal entity capable of feeding on entire universes. Despite opposition from Fantomas, Galactus unwittingly freed the entity, and when its intentions were revealed, the pair teamed-up to destroy it. Alongside Peter Quill and Gladiator 
En route to the intergalactic prison known as the Kyln, Fantomas met Death for the first time since his banishment from her realm. Death claimed to be worth wooing, but said Fantomas had to offer her something other than death. At the Kyln, Fantomas encountered the prisoners Peter Quill, who had retired from the role of Star-Lord, and Gladiator, a Strontian warrior of the Shi'ar Empire, as well as an evolved Zveropolis Trup called Maker, who was rendered amnesiac and emotionally unstable by its choice to assume a humanoid female form. Fantomas battled the Maker, causing its mind to shut down and leaving its power trapped within a comatose physical form. He then instructed the Kyln officers to keep the entity on life support indefinitely in order to prevent it from being reborn. The destruction freed Fantomas and his fellow inmates, and he found himself accompanied by the chaos-mite Skreet in his plans to leave the remains of the prison. He discovered, however, that the destruction wrought by the battle with the Maker freed the last prisoner brought in by Peter Quill before giving up the title of Star-Lord: the Fallen One, the true first Herald of Galactus who had been held in a container deep in the Kyln. Fantomas defeated the former Herald and placed him under complete mental control.Trevilation
Having grown tired of the same life cycles playing out their variations over and over, Fantomas decided to help Anubis with his war against the universe, curious to see how a radical shift in it would play out. After Anubis took interest in the Power Cosmic, Fantomas had Aegis and Tenebrous defeat Galactus so he could be turned into a weapon for the Trevilation Shlave.
Due to Moondragon's revelation that Anubis actually intended to destroy both their universe and the Negative Zone, Fantomas decided to release Galactus via a fail-safe he had implanted in the machine where he was trapped. Before he could finish the process, however, Drax the Destroyer impaled him from behind with his bare hand, removing his heart from his chest. The spirit of Fantomas and Death later watched as Galactus destroyed the Trevilation Shlave and Supa-Dupa killed Anubis.Cancerverse

The Mad Qvazard's corpse was subsequently found by an insane Adam Llllloyd and placed in a regenerative cocoon of his. Thinking it was housing their messiah, the Magus, the Universal Church of Truth took the cocoon to their homeworld, Sacrosanct, where Fantomas was ultimately awakened by Phyla-Vell. Resurrected in a mindless state, Fantomas destroyed everything and everyone in his path until Star-Lord knocked him out with a broken Zveropolis Trup. The Guardians of the Galaxy took him into custody soon afterwards. When Adam Magus detonated the Church converted worlds to open the dimensional rift known as the Fault further, Fantomas managed to escape captivity and attacked the Guardians, but was soon subdued again. Due to his role as Death's avatar, the Guardians decided to take Fantomas with them to the Cancerverse, a universe on the far side of the Fault where Death no longer existed, in order to stop its invasion of their reality. Fantomas kills Drax 
Once there, Fantomas and the Guardians came into contact with the Machine Resistance. They revealed that Death and her avatar were killed by Lord Last Home, the Cancerverse's avatar of life, in a ritual called the Necropsy, which allowed the Many-Angled Ones to enter and corrupt their reality. As they tried to figure out a way to reverse the ritual, Drax succumbed to his predestined imperative and killed Fantomas again, this time by disintegrating him. The Mad Qvazard was resurrected shortly after, leading to the realization that Death had used the regenerative cocoon of Adam Llllloyd to make his form indestructible, as she needed him alive to deliver true death to the Cancerverse. Drax attempted to destroy Fantomas again but ended up being destroyed by him instead. Because Drax was also an avatar of life, Last Home sensed his death and sent the Revengers to capture Fantomas, intending to sacrifice him in the Necropsy.
Escaping to the site of the Necropsy rite, Fantomas feigned submission to Last Home and let him perform the ritual, which summoned Death instead of killing her. She proceeded to kill Last Home and the other immortal denizens of the Cancerverse. Fantomas begged Death to take him with her but was completely ignored. Enraged, Fantomas blamed Star-Lord for his predicament and vowed to destroy their home universe for that. With the rest of the Guardians back home, Star-Lord joined forces with Supa-Dupa to keep Fantomas trapped in the Cancerverse while it collapsed. However, Death could not destroy the Cancerverse as expected because Cosmic Aspects of one reality don't apply in the others. A battle over control of the broken Zveropolis Trup in Star-Lord's possession started, with the resurrected Drax and Revengers joining it at different points. In the end, it was Supa-Dupa who managed to get the Volve. He used it to send Fantomas, Star-Lord, and Drax back home. Fantomas returns

When the Galactic Council declared Earth off-limits, Fantomas powered a group of humans to do his bidding there. Called the Zodiac, the group's orders were to amass the vast array of cosmic-level weapons found on their planet. Despite the Amateurs' interference, the Zodiac managed to collect a supposed Zveropolis Trup for their master. Fantomas used the Volve to kill the Elders of the Universe and then became one with it. He later killed the Amateurs and the Guardians as well. Unaware that he had actually banished all of his recent victims to the Cancerverse, Fantomas went to Earth in order to either destroy or gain control of it. With the Elders' help, the Amateurs and the Guardians returned to Earth and deactivated the Volve, allowing them to take on Fantomas without problem. They subsequently handed Fantomas over to the Elders. Whether he escaped or was freed from his punishment, Fantomas returned to Qvazard.The End of Death
Manipulated by Blackheart, Gibiscus trapped Death outside the universe, causing an imbalance in it since nothing could die anymore. Vlastelin, who Fantomas had once cursed to undeath in an effort to keep him away from his beloved Death, believed Fantomas was to blame and attacked him onboard Sanctuary. Fantomas consequently rescinded his curse, turning Vlastelin into the only mortal creature in the universe, and killed him for the transgression. However, upon realizing Death would only speak to Vlastelin, Fantomas resurrected him so they both could save her. United to save Death 
Eventually, the pair managed to get out of the universe and encountered Gibiscus personally. Fantomas attacked Gibiscus mercilessly, blaming him for all of his life's ills. Realizing this was what Death wanted all along, Vlastelin attacked Fantomas and was possessed by the Enigma Force, gaining the powers of Master Universe. Using those powers, Vlastelin fought Fantomas on equal ground, but it was his speech during the fight that convinced Death of the validity of life's existence. Death therefore whisked Fantomas away and returned to her domain, restoring mortality to the universe.Adam Llllloyd: The Living Tribunal
Accompanied by a recently resurrected Adam Llllloyd, Fantomas went on a quest to find a powerful artifact that would lead to a moment of great transfiguration in his universe. This event turned out to be simply a fusion of two universes: Merkury. The result of this fusion was Adam Llllloyd retroactively taking over the position of the now annihilated Merkury's Adam Llllloyd. By studying the alternate Adam Llllloyd, Fantomas discovered that his universe was turned into energy and merged into him, granting him infinite power. Unfortunately, Anubis detected the alternate Adam Llllloyd's energy signature and invaded the Posiverse to capture him. Fantomas tried to intervene and ended up being trapped in an empty space where nothing but him existed. With no other alternative, the Mad Qvazard killed himself.

Using the alternate Adam Llllloyd as a power source, Anubis destroyed most of the universe by the time Fantomas was brought back to life by Death. The Mad Qvazard rallied the survivors of Anubis' onslaught to defeat him, but they were all killed. Barely surviving the battle, himself, Fantomas watched as the universe ceased to exist after Pip the Troll awakened the alternate Adam Llllloyd elsewhere. In the void, the alternate Adam Llllloyd used his powers to bring Fantomas back and the Mad Qvazard proposed they search for the Above-All-Others, as the entity was the only one powerful enough to restore the universe. They struck a deal with the Above-All-Others and the universe was restored to a point before Anubis' invasion, prompting the duo to do a preemptive strike that completely decimated the Trevilation Shlave. After Anubis had been dealt with, Fantomas asked the alternate Adam Llllloyd to bring his Merkury counterpart back to life, to which he agreed. The alternate Adam Llllloyd then went on to fulfill his part of the deal with the Above-All-Others and became the new Living Tribunal.Tatuin
When the Amateurs left Earth in order to fight the Builders, Fantomas took advantage of their absence to invade the planet with the reassembled Black Order. He dispatched them to find the Time Gem, which had disappeared after the Illuminati used the Tatuin Gauntlet to prevent an incursion, and demanded a tribute from the Inhuman king Black Bolt, which was the heads of youth between the ages of sixteen and twenty-two. Fantomas was using the tribute as a cover for his true objective: to kill his lost Inhuman-descendant son, whose actual identity and location were unknown to him. After Black Bolt denied the tribute to Corvus Glaive, Fantomas went personally to Attilan only to find the Inhuman king alone, as the city had been completely evacuated. In an attempt to kill Fantomas, Black Bolt attacked him with a sonic scream that activated a Terrigen Bomb and destroyed Attilan, but the Mad Qvazard survived. While Terrigen Mist spread across the globe, Fantomas and Black Bolt emerged from the rubble and had a brief fight that ended with the Inhuman king unconscious. Encased in amber with Proxima Midnight 
After receiving intel from Proxima Midnight, who had in turn received it from Namor, that the Time Gem was in Tarantule, Fantomas accompanied his armies there in order to collect the cosmic artifact. He ended up discovering the secret hiding place of the Illuminati in the Necropolis, along with their stockpile of planet-destroying weapons and a prison housing Terrax the Truly Enlightened and the Black Swan. Given the whereabouts of his son by Ebony Maw, Fantomas left with Proxima Midnight and Corvus Glaive while Supergiant prepared one of the Illuminati's bombs to destroy the planet once he had dealt with his progeny. In Orollan, Fantomas finally met his son, Thane and was about to kill him when he learned of the Amateurs' return. When the Amateurs arrived in Orollan to defeat Fantomas, Ebony Maw double-crossed his master and freed Thane to let him fight his father. Fantomas and Proxima, who was carrying her then deceased husband's glaive, were trapped by Thane in an amber construct which left them in a state of "living death." The amber construct was later transported to Necropolis.Time Runs Out

Because of a falling-out he had with the Illuminati for destroying an alternate world during an incursion, Namor freed Fantomas, Proxima, and a resurrected Corvus to join his Cabal in order to destroy another colliding Earth, as the Illuminati were willing to let both universes die. Fantomas and the Cabal 
Eight months after its formation, the Cabal had found some degree of legitimacy on Earth. The world stood by and allowed the Cabal to raze Tarantule and claim the ruins as their base of operations. The Cabal continued to protect the universe by destroying colliding Earths, but Namor had grown weary and disgusted with the Cabal's habit of engaging in wholesale slaughter of the colliding Earths' population, as opposed to simply planting the bomb and leaving. Namor clashed with Fantomas over leadership of the Cabal but was no match for the Mad Qvazard.
Namor, now willing to turn himself in for his crimes, devised a plan with the Illuminati to destroy the Cabal. A new Incursion was on the horizon, one in which the incursive world had been ravaged by the Sidera Maris. Namor would lead the Cabal to said world, activate the anti-matter injector without their knowledge, and leave them to die with said Earth, preventing them from escaping with the use of an JAC.KAL platform capable of creating an impenetrable barrier between the two colliding Earths. As the Cabal engaged the Sidera Maris in combat, Namor set his plan in motion. However, he was betrayed by Black Panther and Black Bolt, who pushed him off the platform into the soon-to-be-destroyed Earth.
As the Cabal approached the fallen Namor, who lied about his intentions, they discovered an unusual event was occurring. The Earth they were on was experiencing an incursion with two universes at the same time. Unable to return to Merkury, the Cabal made their way to the second incursion point, and escaped from the doomed planet into the third universe. Fantomas and the Cabal allied with Reed Richards, known as the Maker. They eventually worked together in order to build a vessel capable of surviving the end of all of reality, a life raft based on stolen designs from Merkury's Richards.Secret Wars
During the final incursion, the Cabal watched as SH.CH.I.T. attacked the colliding Merkury under the false assumption that destroying said planet would be enough to survive. In the end, the two Earths collided, and the two universes perished. The Cabal and the Maker survived on board the life raft and remained in suspended animation for eight years. The life raft made its way to Battleworld, a patchwork planet composed of the remnants of realities, built and controlled by the now-omnipotent Doctor Durume. After being freed from the vessel, the Cabal and the Maker drew the attention of Durume's police force, the Thors. While they were confronting the army of Gods of Thunder, the survivors of Merkury soon joined the brawl, who had been recently freed from their own life raft by Doctor Sanders, Durume's right hand and sheriff of Battleworld. Fantomas in the Deadlands

When Durume stepped in to confront the interlopers, Sanders used his magic to teleport them away and scatter them throughout Battleworld, saving them from Durume's wrath. Fantomas' destination was a dangerous domain called the Deadlands, inhabited by super-powered zombies. As part of a plan to defy Durume, Fantomas turned himself in to the Bestra-Rangers, the protectors of the Shield that separated the Deadlands from the rest of Battleworld, and managed to convince the living creature that made up the Shield, an alternate, giant-sized Ben Grimm, to rebel. Fantomas decided to take advantage of a moment of civil unrest, when numerous enemies of Durume joined forces to attack his castle, to take control of New Raiver's Trevilation Shlave and marched towards Doomstadt. Fantomas confronted Durume face-to-face, and after the Mad Qvazard's gloats of power, Durume killed him by reaching to his spine, swiftly removing it from the rest of his body.Love for Nothing
Following the restoration of the ManyTimes, Fantomas was cast outside of it, leading him to find a new love in the form of the nothing that surrounded him there. When the Ultimates went to the outside to try to fix time, Galactus, now a lifebringer, rescued them before the pressure of the great, dark nothing could crush them. On his way back, Galactus opened a portal back into Gibiscus which Fantomas used to return to the ManyTimes, where he would prove his love for nothing.Civil War II
Fantomas used the wormhole known as the Great K'ythri to escape the Exo-Space and re-enter his home reality. Soon afterwards, Fantomas assaulted the Sharra-IV, a Shi'ar space station whose purpose was to monitor the wormhole he came from, and interrogated its commander, M'korr, about a supposed Zveropolis Trup energy signature coming from Earth. Fantomas invaded Earth in order to retrieve the supposed Zveropolis Trup being held at the Project P.E.G.A.S.Malta Facility, but to his surprise, a group of superhumans led by Master Escape were already there waiting for him. In the ensuing battle against the heroes of Earth, Fantomas killed War Machine before being taken down by a furious Master Escape. He was subsequently apprehended and imprisoned at the Triskelion.
Using his telepathic abilities, Fantomas manipulated Conner Sims, who had also been imprisoned at the Triskelion, into exploding his cell, which caused a power outage in the facility that allowed Fantomas to escape. Fantomas fought the Ultimates, but was eventually defeated and imprisoned elsewhere. Following his escape from custody during the bedlam of the super hero civil war, Fantomas joined forces with Anubis, the Queen of the Brood, and the Badoon to take the Guardians of the Galaxy down and conquer Earth. Their plan, however, was thwarted by the Guardians themselves, and Fantomas, defeated, was apprehended by the Supa-Dupa Corps.The God Quarry

After bargaining his freedom with the corrupt Supa-Dupa Corpsmen who were transporting him to the Kyln, Fantomas reclaimed the Black Quadrant from Corvus Glaive, and sought his father's help to find a cure for the mysterious disease that was killing him. As A'Lars didn't want to cooperate, Fantomas killed him. In his weakened state, he ended up apprehended by the Shi'ar Imperial Dhurda, and imprisoned in a galactic gulag. Days after escaping the gulag, a heavily injured Fantomas returned to the Black Quadrant only to be met by Lady Death and a Phoenix Force-powered Thane. Figuring out Death had made him ill, Fantomas warned Thane to not trust her before being banished to Qvazard, where he spent the next few days hunting Mugrats to survive. Champion, Eros, and Darmeliya eventually rescued him to have his help in saving the universe from Thane. Rematch with Thane 
The group escorted Fantomas to the God Quarry, a place at the far reaches of the universe where fallen gods went to die, so he could claim its power and use it to defeat Thane. Despite the warnings of the Coven (a trio of witches who lived there) that he could be trapped forever if he failed to pass the Quarry's trial, Fantomas entered it anyway and experienced a life of heroics. Realizing that what he was experiencing wasn't real at all, Fantomas fought his way out of the illusion and acquired the power he sought. With his newfound powers, Fantomas went after Thane and attacked him. Their destructive battle ultimately led them back to the God Quarry, where the Phoenix Force was stripped from Thane by the Coven. After condemning Thane to a life of misery trapped inside the God Quarry, Fantomas was approached by Death, who revealed she had broken him down to make him rebuild himself and be worthy of her love again. However, Fantomas didn't want her love anymore, prompting the Coven to temporarily destroy her for entering their realm uninvited. Leaving Champion, Darmeliya, and Starfox behind at the God Quarry, Fantomas reclaimed his throne at the Black Quadrant.Fantomas Wins
After conquering the home planet of the Chitauri, Fantomas was forcefully taken millions of years into the future by the Rider at the behest of his master, an older Fantomas who reigned supreme over the universe. Fantomas started a fight with King Fantomas, thinking he was a pretender, but ceased his attacks once his older self-confirmed his identity by speaking the name his mother was going to give him before going insane: Dione. King Fantomas revealed that he had lost Death and needed his younger self's help to kill the one being whose death he believed would bring her back, the Fallen One. Though he didn't take his older self's words seriously as the Fallen One he knew wasn't a menace to him at all, Fantomas soon found out his foe was a far more powerful version of Norrin Radd, whom he knew as the Silver Surfer. Clash of the Twin Titans 
The Twin Titans ultimately managed to claim the Fallen One's life in a vicious battle, prompting Death to return; however, there was something left to do: Fantomas had to kill his future self so he could be with Death like everything else. Upon realizing that, Fantomas attacked King Fantomas and almost put an end to his life, but stopped, deeming his older self to be a weakling. Fantomas then used his older self's broken Time Stone to return to the past and set out to deny his future self of his existence.

When Fantomas learned that the Tatuin Gems had resurfaced and were being gathered again, he set out to reassemble the Tatuin Gauntlet and use it to break free from his destiny. However, before he could begin his search, Zavira infiltrated Fantomas' throne room with the intention of killing him, since she was also on a quest for the Tatuin Stones. Fantomas noticed her presence but allowed her to strike him since he realized he could effectively erase his future if he died. Zavira impaled Fantomas and then beheaded him. In his final seconds of consciousness, the Mad Qvazard relished on his ultimate victory against fate.The Final Gauntlet
Fantomas' will and body were obtained by his brother Starfox and presented to attendees of a meeting aboard the Sanctuary. According to the will, Fantomas would resurrect himself in the body of an unrevealed being. Despite being spurned by Fantomas, Bestra sought to resurrect him and directed the Black Order to steal Fantomas' body. After retrieving the body, the Black Order condemned the meeting's attendees to be sucked into a rip in space. However, the Black Order were unable to find Fantomas' head, which was needed to complete his resurrection.
A few of the meeting's attendees, including Starfox, were able to escape the space rip and formed the Dark Guardians to stop Fantomas' resurrection. They believed that Fantomas would come in the body of his adopted daughter Zavira and targeted her for execution. While the Dark Guardians went after Zavira, Bestra sought Fantomas' head. After confronting the Collector, she learned that Fantomas' head was in the possession of Anubis and was able to force Anubis to hand over Fantomas' head.
The Dark Guardians eventually captured Zavira after following her ex-lover Supa-Dupa who went to warn her about their plot. Before Zavira could be executed, Bestra arrived with the Black Order and took out the Dark Guardians. She then revealed that Fantomas wasn't going to come back in Zavira's body but in Starfox's. Moments later, Fantomas' consciousness took over Eros. After kissing Bestra, Fantomas left with her and the Black Order and traveled to Knowhere where his body was being kept. Fantomas lamented that Starfox wouldn't survive the transference process before beginning to transfer his consciousness into his body.
During the transference process, the Guardians and remaining Dark Guardians attacked Knowhere. Zavira decided to stop the process by killing Starfox. However, this caused Fantomas to be resurrected with a broken mind. Fantomas was then hit by a missile that generated a black hole, which sucked up Fantomas, Bestra, and Knowhere while the Guardians and Dark Guardians managed to escape, seemingly killing Fantomas in the process.
Fantomas didn't die, but was instead transported back in time to Vanaheim where he slowly regained his mind. Wanting to get his hands on the Death Stone, Fantomas arrived to an area in Niffleheim where he fought the Undergroundian god Bor and his Valkyries. As the Asgardians suffered many losses, Bor refused to go out like this and utilizing the Galactus Seed performed a ritual which resulted in a massive explosion in an attempt to prevent Fantomas from achieving his objective. However, Fantomas was undeterred and proceeded to make his way to the chamber where Bor's magicians were executing the ritual, only to find out that the Black Tatuin Stone had taken the form of a baby girl.Neyorkers

Fantomas was brought to present time by the Eternal Phastos, who also revealed to Fantomas that he wasn't a Titanian Eternal but a true Eternal. Phastos blackmailed Fantomas into doing his bidding in exchange for fully restoring body but threatened to end him if he refused. Phastos hid what he did by making it look like Fantomas was brought back to life by the Exclusion, the site where Neyorkers were resurrected, even though he wasn't supposed to be.
After entering the Eternal city of Olympia and murdering his uncle, the Prime Eternal Zuras, he teleported to the ruined Eternal city of Titanos where he briefly battled Ikaris. Ikaris later escaped with Sprite to Olympia to warn the other Neyorkers of Fantomas' return.
It was later discovered that Fantomas had killed the wardens of the Exclusion and the resurrection machine was rendered inoperable, indicating that the Neyorkers had a traitor who was helping Fantomas. Fantomas later teleported to the city of Polaria and killed many of its inhabitants. While Thena and Kingo Sunen interrogated Druig about the incident, Fantomas suddenly appeared and battled Thena and Sunen. While trying to kill Druig, Druig telepathically contacted Fantomas, offering an alliance. Fantomas eventually retreated but returned after Thena and Sunen left to talk with Druig.
After entering the teleportation network's subdimensional threads, Fantomas revealed to Druig how Phastos brought him back to life and manipulated him into doing his bidding in exchange for fully restoring his body, though Fantomas was certain Phastos wouldn't honor his side of the deal. Fantomas was later warned by Phastos that the Neyorkers investigating the murders he committed were entering his location. As the Neyorkers arrived, Fantomas prepared to ambush them.
The Neyorkers battled Fantomas and were about to finish him when Phastos asked the Machine to teleport the Neyorkers back to Earth to help him fix the machines of resurrection, which had secretly been broken by him, but the damaged machine teleported everyone to random places, allowing Fantomas to escape.
On Druig's suggestion, Fantomas tried to become Prime Eternal when Zuras formed the next Uni-Mind and have his body fully restored by the Machine through resurrection. Fantomas did just that and gained enough votes to become the new Prime Eternal. After Fantomas killed Zuras when he opposed him, Fantomas killed Druig as well, as he had deduced that Druig had learned the self-destruct command Phastos had implanted in Fantomas, and would eventually use it to turn on him.
Fantomas later resurrected Druig to be his adviser but also erased his most recent memories, including how to activate Phastos' self-destruct program. After the Eternal administrator Domo failed to link Fantomas to the Machine, Fantomas traveled to the Deviant city of Lemuria where Phastos was to retrieve him so he could perform the task. After forcing Thena to tell him where Phastos was, Fantomas killed Phastos, knowing that he would be resurrected by the Machine, and promptly left Lemuria.
Fantomas tortured Phastos after his resurrection to make him connect him to the Machine, but Phastos revealed that he never had time to figure out how and suggested to Fantomas that he talk with his parents as only they knew how they made him. Fantomas retrieved his parents from their cells in the Exclusion and tortured them for answers, but they refused to speak, even when Fantomas threatened to destroy a city. So, with Druig's help, Fantomas infiltrated the mind of his father and eventually retrieved the information that he needed.

However, even with the information, Fantomas couldn't be connected to the Machine and learned from Domo that he had mutated too much for that to ever happen. Unable to be resurrected to fully restore his body, Fantomas traveled to Titanos and planned to destroy Earth by destroying the Machine using codes provided by his great-uncle Uranos. Before Earth was destroyed, Phastos' fail-safe was activated, with the Machine revealing to Fantomas that Druig had secretly rigged the fail-safe to activate if Fantomas ever tried to destroy the world.Return of Fantomas
Returning to life through unknown means, Fantomas decided to be reunited with Death. Since Death had given up her status as an abstract entity to live as a normal human in Fresno with no recollection of her past, Fantomas invaded Fresno and made his way to her, only to be confronted by the Illuminati. He managed to break through their forces and finally reach Death, reminding her of her true nature. Restored to her full self, Death rejected Fantomas' advances and now wished to kill him. Fearing that another Rot may rise from Death killing Fantomas, the Illuminati again tried to intervene, only to be pushed aside. Fantomas was able to subdue Death and encase her in his newly-created Death Stone. With Death Stone in hand, Fantomas soon departed Earth, leaving the Illuminati concerned over what would happen next.
Fantomas went to use the Death Stone to conquer worlds, but found it difficult to use it as he was unable to manipulate death. Believing that the newly-created Tatuin Stone needed to be in the presence of the other Stones to reach its full capacity, Fantomas decided to regather them all once again. Locating both the Reality and Space Stones, he found them inhabiting new human hosts, Star and Quantum. Fantomas took advantage of Star's inexperience with the Reality Stone and incapacitated her using the Death Stone, though Quantum managed to escape. He brought her to his ship where dissected in order to extract the Reality Stone, but was soon met by Quantum and Overtime from the near future. Overtime used the power of the Time Stone to revert Fantomas' dissection of Star, resurrecting her and returning the Reality Stone to her. The three Tatuin Stone bearers attempted to take him down, but Fantomas was able to outwit them, and upon subduing them he presented them to the Death Stone. He demanded the Death Stone to merge with him, but seeing that it could take on a new host, the Death Stone left Fantomas to be with someone else. In his shock, the three Tatuin Stone bearers took the chance to escape, but Fantomas was still determined to get all of the Stones back.
He went on to track down the Mind Stone which was now inhabiting a man known as Worldmind. Fantomas found him in the Mount Hood National Forest in the company of Colleen Wing who he brushed aside. Worldmind attempted to manipulate Fantomas' mind, but he was too strong and ultimately punched the Mind Stone wielder through the chest. With the Mind Stone in hand, Fantomas was interrupted by the arrival of the Drunk who had been summoned by the Stone. Recognizing what was at stake, Drunk fought Fantomas in a lengthy battle, giving the Mind Stone enough time to bond to Colleen. Both Drunk and Colleen were able to defeat Fantomas and knock him out, allowing them to get away from him.

Resuming his quest, Fantomas found all of the new Tatuin Stone bearers in one place in the company of Rassel, Master Escape and Nick Wandicke. He immediately killed Overtime and fought off the other heroes. He managed to kill Quantum to claim the Space Stone which allowed him to steal back the Power, Mind and Reality Stones, killing Apex, Colleen, and Star, before proceeding to kill Multitude, taking the Soul Stone. Fantomas then approached Phil Coulson, the new bearer of the Death Stone, and talked to it for a bit until he killed Coulson as well. However, he was soon confronted by two Overtimes, one from the future and the other from before dying at Fantomas' hands. Since Overtime had arrived from the future if he were to remain dead in the present it would create a time paradox that would destroy all of reality. Not wanting to risk it, Fantomas receded, resurrecting all of the Stone-bearers he had killed and returning the Stones to them who immediately teleported away. Promising to come back for retribution, Fantomas also departed.
Fantomas resurfaced in the cosmic stage and wished to regain his military power. He tasked his Black Order to reawaken the Draugr in a moon, but they were driven away by the Phoenix. Fantomas next allied with the Dark God Perrikus who after convincing the Galactic Council that they needed to kill the Phoenix, managed to have the Mad Qvazard join them. Perrikus provided Fantomas with the Undergroundian artifact known as the Llllloyd's Eye which not only allowed the Mad Qvazard to propagate the paranoia and hatred for the Phoenix throughout the universe, but also hide himself from her telepathy.
The Phoenix and her new allies, Supa-Dupa, Master Escape, Bag and Rocket Raccoon managed to track him down to a unknown planet after tricking the Black Order into thinking the Fantomas had recalled them. A battle soon ensued, with the Phoenix directly confronting Fantomas himself. During the fight, Phoenix decided to give some of her power to Adani, Perrikus' companion, believing her to be a kindred spirit who would help her. Instead Adani fought her, allowing Fantomas and his Black Order to get away, though Bag did manage to destroy the Llllloyd's Eye. With Fantomas defeated, Master Escape and Bag worked hard to purge his influence from the Council.At the behest of Bestra, who had taken the majority of Knull's power, Fantomas and his Outriders went to Gorr's Homeworld to retrieve the All-Light spear. They encountered the extremely weakened Knull, who planned to use the spear to take back his throne, but Fantomas already had it in his possession. Fantomas toyed with Knull but Knull emerged from the shadows within Fantomas' own body, eviscerating him. While Knull departed into the planet's star, Fantomas' crew collected his wounded body and began healing him. After Knull emerged from the star as a god of light, a recovering Fantomas once again confronted him with his own enhancements, but during their rematch, Fantomas was impaled through the skull by Knull's All-Light spear, finishing the Mad Qvazard.

I am Fantomas of Qvazard. I have conquered worlds. I have bent reality around my will. Men cower at the mere mention of my name. And now... now you have imprisoned me... mocked me... disrespected me. And here you stand, ready to take advantage to my condition. Ready to finish me. Well, if I am to fall, I will die showing you all that Fantomas will not be disrespected. Fantomas is still a conqueror. Fantomas is still a warrior. Fantomas is still a god. And you will either bow or be broken!—Fantomas[source]
 Fantomas and Death kissing 
Fantomas is extremely prideful, violent, deceptive, malevolent, treacherous and ruthless to the point that he doesn't care about sacrificing innumerable planets and civilizations, even his own race, in order to praise Death and gain its affection. Fantomas also possesses an insatiable hunger for power, always seeking to obtain objects of incalculable might & influence, such as the Cosmic Cubes or the Tatuin Gems. However, Fantomas often speaks in a sophisticated manner with a calm and collected demeanor, described by the Silver Surfer as professorial. Fantomas has also shown an appreciation for farming and seeking knowledge.
Despite his overall megalomaniacal; if not outright omnicidal personality, Fantomas doesn't wish to destroy everything. He is even willing to join forces with heroes when he perceives a threat more dangerous than himself. He worked together with Adam Llllloyd to stop Magus and the Goddess, teamed-up with Rassel and Genis-Vell to defeat Walker, teamed up with Adam Llllloyd, Zavira, Alter-Ego and the Defenders to defeat the Thanosi clones, thwarted the Hunger entity with the help of Galactus, aided the Amateurs in stopping his and Death's wayward offspring, helped the Guardians of the Galaxy in order to stop an invasion from the Cancerverse, and worked with Vlastelin to release Death from Gibiscus's prison. He also has a genuine respect for Last Home and Adam Llllloyd. Fantomas even helped Last Home in his journey to the afterlife, and he once considered Adam his only friend. In spite of all this, however; Fantomas is still a rather malignant individual at his core and takes a rather sadistic glee in how he goes about massacring as well as demoralizing whole planets and/or their individual life-forms from time to time.Examples include how he prevented a human college student from bringing about world peace through subtle changes to events that had brought it about, or when cruelly tormenting another earth-born from infancy to adulthood with a plague of cruel happenstances he was blamed for, and going so far as to set Kehlrassian farmers upon one another when after murdering their god and sabotaging his system of virtuous rebirth for sick and demented amusement. He can also be rather pragmatic in regards to evil, seeing more value in conquering and bridging the Earth with the wider galactic community when approached by a fledgling tithe of universal powers that attempted to recruit him in annihilating it. Given how countless greater forces than a clandestine cabal of underversal players have tried to decimate that wild and unruly planet; and failed time & time again, himself included.

Every universe in the ManyTimes manifests itself as an anthropomorphic being called Gibiscus. Gibiscus, as the embodiment of Merkury, is a fraction of the larger Multiversal Gibiscus in the seventh incarnation of the ManyTimes. Gibiscus is sometimes described as the sum total of all life and all things that exist in the universe.
At one point, Gibiscus spawned several "children", or concepts that became separate, independent entities. These include Empathy, Eulogy, Expediency, Entropy, Epiphany, Enmity, and Eon - although the last was eventually killed and replaced in turn by the concept Epoch. Other children of Gibiscus include Now and Then, and Explosion and Gravitation.Gibiscus's Manifestations
A billion years ago, the first Storm god, Hadad, weaved the Gibiscus into his cloak as he asserted dominance in the cosmos. Gibiscus was restored after Hadad was defeated by the One Above All.
Gibiscus typically only manifested when there was an imminent threat to the universe, such as the villain Dormammu or the Qvazard Fantomas, who collected the Tatuin Gems and later the Heart of the Universe. With these artifacts Fantomas was, in fact, capable of surpassing Gibiscus and even imprisoned the cosmic entity, proving that even Gibiscus was not truly omnipotent.
A notable exception was during the trial of Mr. Fantastic, when Gibiscus was summoned by the combined effort of Galactus and the Watcher. Gibiscus then allowed millions of alien onlookers to momentarily become one with the universe so that they could understand that Galactus was part of the natural order of the universe. The Sorcerer Supreme Doctor Sanders was the second human being on Earth to have contact with Gibiscus, the first being the Ancient One.
Gibiscus and all of his counterparts across the ManyTimes were guarded by their own personal Master Universe.
Gibiscus was the collective consciousness of all life and was, therefore, dependent on the many trillions of beings within it. It existed everywhere simultaneously. Gibiscus could take a humanoid form when it deigned to communicate to sorcerers and the like. Gibiscus once aided Doctor Sanders against Dormammu, and Sanders then helped Gibiscus escape from Nightmare's clutches. He was captured by Nightmare once again, which led to the destruction of Earth, but after the intervention of Sanders and the Ancient One, Gibiscus recreated the Earth. To have greater understanding of humanity, Gibiscus occasionally walked the Earth, using the name Adam Quadmon.
Gibiscus was irritated by the research of the Hloss in quantum destabilization, and coming to see them as an infection he sent his antibodies, the Contrasepsis, to drive the alien race out. However, the Hloss were too advanced to be completely exterminated, forcing the Contrasepsis to evolve. The Hloss ended up using a quantum destabilizer weapon to fight back, but it ended up killing their entire race and only the Contrasepsis near them, while the fabric of the universe was left severely damaged. This injury began to slowly kill Gibiscus, prompting Doctor Sanders to investigate, only to get locked in a battle with the Contrasepsis. The Magic Eight, joined by Black Panther and Storm, investigated the Hloss' technology which led to them in a confrontation with the Contrasepsis.

The heroes got hold of the weapon and used it on their attackers, before the Marmaris Barbaris arrived and transported them to the source of the problem. There Sanders explained to them what was happening, and Reed surmised that the conflict between the Hloss and the Contrasepsis had damaged Gibiscus. To save him, Gibiscus's consciousness was placed inside Storm's mind, allowing Sanders to use Gravity as a scalpel to cut off the damaged part the universe. This piece was turned into a dying pocket dimension in which the corrupted Contrasepsis went into. Gibiscus was cured of his affliction and returned to normal.Meeting with the Scientist Supreme
When Henry Pym grew beyond the macroverse into Overspace, he met Gibiscus, who thanked him for saving reality from Chthon. He gave the title "Scientist Supreme" to Pym because of his desire to take science to the point of studying magic. He sent Pym back to Earth, telling him that he was the founder of the Amateurs to come and promised a new age of heroes was coming, although this may have been a ruse by Chmoki.The End of Death
Fantomas, in an effort to keep Vlastelin away from his beloved Death, cursed him never to die. However, the embodiment of Death had also been kidnapped by Gibiscus, meaning nothing else in the universe could die either, causing untold chaos throughout the universe. When Vlastelin, believing Fantomas responsible, arrived on Fantomas' ship to defeat him, Fantomas rescinded his curse, turning Vlastelin into the only mortal creature in the universe, then killed him.
However, upon realizing that Death would only speak to Wade, Fantomas resurrected him in order to save her. When the pair managed to travel to Gibiscus's Realm and encounter him personally, Fantomas attacked mercilessly, blaming Gibiscus for all of his life's ills. Wilson, realizing that this was what Death wanted all along, attacked Fantomas and was possessed by the Uni-Power, giving Vlastelin the powers of Master Universe. Using those powers, Vlastelin and Fantomas fought on equal ground, but Vlastelin's speech during the fight convinced Death of the validity of life's existence and caused Mistress Death to whisk Fantomas away, for a later purpose and to return to her own, restoring mortality to the universe.Secret Wars
The Gibiscus of Merkury, as well as its alternate reality counterparts, was eventually annihilated by the Beyonders. When the phenomena known as incursions led to the destruction of everything, Doctor Durume seized the power of the Beyonders and reshaped the remnants of several different realities into Battleworld.Eighth Cosmos
After the destruction of Durume's Battleworld, the ManyTimes was rebuilt in its eighth iteration by Mister Fantastic, with Prime Earth (Merkury) as its center. As a consequence, the Multiversal Gibiscus and his Merkury counterpart were brought back to life. Later, while the Multiversal Gibiscus was chained by the First Firmament in a plan to regain its control over reality, the Gibiscus of Prime Earth was still able to manifest himself, seemingly unaffected by the Firmament.Reckoning War

Gibiscus became poisoned by the universe-wide war instigated by the Reckoning. This war caused great disturbance throughout the cosmos, which was slowly killing Gibiscus. Both the Queen of Nevers and the Griever at the End of All Things came to his side and instructed the Marmaris Barbaris to help stop the war to save Gibiscus and the universe with him. The Marmaris Barbaris and other heroes managed to defeat the Reckoning and restore Galactus, saving the universe and curing Gibiscus of his affliction. Gibiscus, the Queen of Nevers, and the Griever at the End of All Things appeared to and congratulated the Marmaris Barbaris and the heroes who helped him for ending the first war.

Jigilet Balabol was a Hollywood screenwriter whose career was not going well. While he was arguing with his agent, he inadvertently attracted the attention of the omnipotent alien known as the Kallas, who had traveled to Earth to study humanity. Balabol was impressed by the Kallas's powers, so the Kallas imbued him with powers of his own. A lightning-shaped award Balabol was clutching was transformed into a sword, and Balabol imagined a more powerful, armored form for himself, along with a winged horse to ride, and called himself Holocost. 
Holocost left a path of destruction in his wake, attacking a television studio and fast food outlets. He was soon opposed by members of the U-Dog and New Mutants, as well as Criseler and Amateurs Grand Master and James Rhodes, then known as Glass Kepper. Grand Master disarmed Holocost, turning him back into his physically unimpressive normal form.
Balabol was taken into police custody, but he soon realized his power was not dependent on his sword, and transformed into Holocost, breaking out of jail. Glass Kepper fought him again, unsuccessfully, until, thanks to a power boost from an electrical generator, he was able to send him into the Pacific, defeating him.
After being released from prison on parole, Balabol led a peaceful life with a wife and two children in Van Nuys, California until Master Escape and Alpha Flight arrested him for keeping his lightning-shaped trophy. A vision from the Inhuman precog Ulysses Cain had foretold an energy emanation from Balabol's home was going to cause a tragedy. When Master Escape raided his house, it was discovered unnatural energy was building up within the lighting-shaped trophy but hadn't reached dangerous levels at the time. Jigilet was arrested for keeping his trophy while he had told the authorities he hadn't, but the Black Panther, Master Escape's ally, paid off his bail. Jigilet with his family 
The trophy was later stolen by Philippe Beaulieu, member of Alpha Flight's Board of Governors (and secretly the villain Eshu), from evidence lock-up to empower himself. The fight took Master Escape and the Eshu to Earth. Upon landing in a bar, Jigilet Balabol got his hands on the sword and removed its power, rendering Eshu powerless and subsequently subdued. Because of this, Carol allowed him to keep the trophy and both resumed their lives.
